# Consistency pass before 1.0.0 Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A team that installs Horizon Watch 1.0.0 meets one shape for each concept: one environment
type instead of a colour plus a production flag, one Horizon URL as the only address, one evaluated
state with one wording and tone, one set of wall KPIs, one formatter per kind of value, one
vocabulary in English and Italian, one environment form, one set of shared primitives, no stored or
sent data that only repeats another fact, documentation and version that match the product, and a
secret-free configuration export and import.

**Architecture:** Nine batches run in order on `release/1.0`, each one commit with
`composer ci:check` green: the two schema changes first (type and address), then state and KPIs,
formatters, vocabulary, pages and forms, primitives, data trimming, docs and version, and
configuration export and import. The server stays the single source of each fact (Data objects
generated into TypeScript, server-side judgement and counts, `HorizonUrl` and `OutboundUrl`,
`Duration`), while the client keeps only shared helpers (`lib/environments.ts`, `readings.ts`,
`lib/monitoring.ts`, `lib/datetime.ts`, `useWallKpis`) and shared Vue primitives. Every renamed
English string moves its `lang/it.json` key in the same batch, guarded by `TranslationsTest` and by
source-scanning Pest tests that keep removed patterns out.

**Tech Stack:** PHP 8.5, Laravel 13, Fortify, Inertia 3 with Vue 3.5 and TypeScript 5,
spatie/laravel-data 4 with laravel-typescript-transformer 3 (generated `App.*` types), Laravel
Wayfinder, Tailwind CSS 4 with the Nocturne stylesheet (`resources/css/nocturne.css`),
laravel-vue-i18n (`lang/it.json`), Pest 4, Vitest through vite-plus, vue-tsc, Pint, Larastan,
PostgreSQL, Docker Compose / Sail (every PHP and Node command runs in the `laravel.test` container).

**Spec:** docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-consistency-pass-design.md

## Global Constraints

- Migrations already shipped in v0.1.0 are never edited; every schema change is a new migration with a working `down()` where data allows (new migrations are `2026_10_16_000001`–`000003` in Batch 1 and `2026_10_16_000004`–`000005` in Batch 7).
- The webhook v1 payload keeps its keys and types. Only the free-text `summary` changes wording (durations), noted in the CHANGELOG.
- Every changed English source string renames its `lang/it.json` key in the same commit; `TranslationsTest` must stay green (no unused, no missing keys).
- `composer ci:check` green after every batch, run in the Sail container.
- Status colours stay reserved; identity colours stay in the cool range (`PRODUCT.md`).
- Owner decision, production vs colour: One field, **environment type**. The colour follows the type. "Production" means type `production`. The `is_production` flag and the `worker` choice disappear.
- Owner decision, application domain: **Removed.** The only address is each environment's full Horizon dashboard URL.
- Owner decision, duration notation: **Spaced**: `45 s`, `17 min`, `1 h 5 min`, `2 d 3 h`, everywhere (panel, emails, webhook `summary`). Compact form only on chart axes.
- Owner decision, is `degraded` healthy? **No.** Healthy means status `active`; everything else with a status needs attention.
- Owner decision, configuration export and import: applications, environments and alert rules; both panel and command line; import shows a preview and lets the admin choose to update or skip existing items; nothing is ever deleted; environments that need a basic-auth password arrive with collection paused and a "password needed" mark (Italian: "Password da inserire"); secrets never leave the panel; one JSON document per organization, UTF-8, at most 1 MB.
- Default (owner may override), Italian role names: Translate all four: Proprietario, Amministratore, Membro, Osservatore. Record the rule in the CONTRIBUTING glossary.
- Default (owner may override), time zones: 1.0 labels zones where times are entered or shown; moving the zone to organization settings is deferred.
- Default (owner may override), release version: Bare `1.0.0` in the app, `/health` and the User-Agent; git tags stay `v*`.
- Default (owner may override), internal "anomaly" identifiers: Renamed to "alert" now (permission value, policy ability, component and config names), with a config fallback for `wall_anomalies`.
- Default (owner may override), alert-rule scopes: Stay keyed by environment name (unchanged).
- Default (owner may override), alert text authorship: Client renders, with the shared keys and formatters of theme 6.
- Default (owner may override), `environments.last_polled_at`, `ManageCredentials` gate: Left as they are for 1.0.
- Default (owner may override), action rows: Right-aligned, secondary then primary.
- Out of scope: moving the time zone to organization settings, rule scopes by type, `last_polled_at`, merging `ManageCredentials`, server-authored alert text, chat channels.
- Plan-wide (every part): batches run in order 1 to 9 on `release/1.0`, one local commit each; `docs/superpowers/plans/` is never staged; no step pushes, merges or tags (pushing `release/1.0`, merging to `main` and tagging `v1.0.0` follow CONTRIBUTING → Releasing once all nine batches are in; the owner has authorized that release step, merge to `main` and tag `v1.0.0`, after Batch 9 is reviewed and green).

## Review Focus

- A base Horizon URL pasted with an API path, a trailing slash or capitals (wizard first row, Add environment base, e.g. `HTTPS://Shop.Example.com/horizon/api/stats/`): every suggested URL carries the dashboard path the server stores (`https://staging.shop.example.com/horizon`), and a Horizon served at `/api` keeps it. Pinned in Task 1.6 (`environments.test.ts`).
- A legacy Horizon URL saved before 1.0 with credentials and capitals inside (`https://monitor:…@Production.Example.com/horizon/api`): the Add environment page and the application list never carry the userinfo, and the derived domain is the lower-case host. Pinned in Task 1.4 (`ApplicationFormPagesTest`).
- The first save after the upgrade of an environment whose stored URL is untidy (`https://Production.Example.com/horizon/api/`, password on file): it goes through without retyping the password, stores `https://production.example.com/horizon`, and keeps both the password and the current reading. Pinned in Task 1.4 (`EnvironmentCrudTest`).
- Enter pressed in a field of a form that now wraps other controls (wizard, Add / Edit environment, dialogs, settings): it submits that form and never presses another button, because every `<button>` declares its `type`. Pinned in Task 5.13 (`PagesAndFormsTest`).
- An environment renamed on Edit: its slug and links stay, and the alert overrides of the new name apply instead of those of the old one, as the new name hint promises. Pinned in Task 5.7 (`EnvironmentRulesOnPagesTest`).

## Batch 1: Environment type and one Horizon address

Goal: every environment gets one **type** (`production`, `preprod`, `staging`, `development`,
`testing`, `demo`) that decides its identity colour and whether it is production, replacing the
`color` column, the `is_production` flag and `App\Enums\EnvironmentColor`; and an environment's
full Horizon dashboard URL becomes the only address the product asks for, stores and calls,
replacing `applications.host`, the wizard's "Horizon path" field and
`HostWithoutSchemeOrCredentials`. The server normalises Horizon URLs (`App\Support\HorizonUrl`)
and checks them, like webhook addresses, with one outbound rule (`App\Rules\OutboundUrl`). The
domain shown next to an application is derived from its environments' URLs. The batch ends with
both schema changes migrated (with working `down()`), the seeder, factories, smoke script and
CHANGELOG upgrade notes updated, `composer ci:check` green and one commit on `release/1.0`.

Spec themes covered: **1. Where Horizon lives** and **2. Environment type replaces colour and
production flag** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-consistency-pass-design.md`), plus the
CHANGELOG upgrade notes for those two themes (theme 19 lists them). README changes for these
themes (Horizon URL check at save, environment type, no application domain) stay in Batch 8 as
theme 19 assigns them.

Preconditions (once per machine, from the repo root
`/home/mmarretti@enegan.locale/MyProjects/horizon-watch`):

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec -T pgsql psql -U sail -d laravel -c 'CREATE DATABASE testing' || true
```

Commit policy: the tasks of this batch are committed together at the end (Task 1.12). Between
tasks only the filtered tests named in each task are expected to pass; the full suite and the
type checks are green again at Task 1.12.

Decisions taken where the spec leaves a detail open (each is restated in its task):

- `alerts.environment_type` keeps the nullability of the column it renames: `environment_color`
  was created `not null` in `2026_09_18_000003`, so the renamed column stays `not null` (the
  registry's "nullable like the old column" resolves to "like the old column").
- A colour outside the seven known values, and the old `worker` colour without the flag, map to
  `staging`. A new environment whose name suggests no type also gets `staging` ("never defaults
  to `production` unless its name suggests it").
- `HorizonUrl::normalize` strips a trailing `/api` or `/api/...` only when at least one path
  segment precedes it (the pattern `HorizonTarget::suggestedDashboardUrl` uses), so a Horizon
  served at `/api` is not cut; `HorizonTarget::apiUrl` already treats a bare trailing `/api` at
  call time. Page suffixes such as `/dashboard` or `/failed/...` are not stripped at save,
  because a Horizon path may end in those words; the connection test keeps suggesting them.
- A URL carrying a query string or a fragment is only trimmed and lower-cased by the
  normaliser, never cut, so the validator still refuses it. The default port is not removed.
- Existing stored URLs are not rewritten by a migration; they are normalised the next time the
  environment is saved.
- `OutboundUrl` judges only `http`/`https` addresses: anything else is left to the
  `url:http,https` rule placed before it in both rule lists, so one fault never shows two
  messages. It stops at its first failure (credentials, then query or fragment, then network).
- The derived domain is computed from the environments the viewer may see (managers: every
  environment of the application), so a member limited to non-production never learns the
  production host. "First environment" means the lowest id (creation order).
- The URL suggestion treats a row as production when its **name** suggests production
  (`suggestType(name) === 'production'`), which keeps the registry signature
  `suggestHorizonUrl(baseUrl, baseName, name)`.
- The Edit environment page never changes the type when the name changes; only the wizard and
  Add environment follow the name, until the type is picked by hand (`typeEdited`).
- One follow rule serves every prefilled field (`followSuggestion` and `leavesSuggestion` in
  `lib/environments.ts`): the wizard's further URL rows, the Add environment URL (through the
  composable `useSuggestedHorizonUrl`) and the type that follows the name. A URL field stops
  following once the user types a URL other than the suggestion, and follows again if the user
  types the suggestion back.
- The wall's environment chips become **type** chips (one chip per type present, in enum order,
  labelled from `WallPageData::$types`); the query parameter becomes `?type=`.
- `environments/Show.vue` drops the `mastersPath` hint instead of receiving the path from the
  server.
- The `--env-demo` token keeps its current value (`oklch(0.8 0.09 212)`, the cyan of the
  palette); tokens are renamed, not recoloured, and `--env-worker` is removed.
- The demo seeder keeps its environment names; `worker-batch` gets type `staging`, like the
  migration does.

New shared names introduced by this batch (later batches consume them as written):

- PHP: `App\Support\HorizonUrl::host(string $url): ?string`;
  `App\Data\Applications\EnvironmentFormData::attributes(): array<string, string>` (validation
  attribute names; `horizonUrl` → "Horizon URL");
  `App\Models\Application::primaryEnvironment(\Illuminate\Support\Collection $environments): ?Environment`;
  `App\Rules\OutboundUrl::carriesCredentials(string): bool`,
  `OutboundUrl::carriesQueryOrFragment(string): bool`, protected message hooks
  `credentialsMessage()`, `queryMessage()`, `blockedMessage()` (`App\Rules\WebhookUrl` extends
  `OutboundUrl`); `App\Rules\UrlWithoutCredentials` and `App\Rules\UrlWithoutQueryOrFragment` are
  deleted.
- Data property names: `EnvironmentData::$type`, `EnvironmentFormData::$type`,
  `EnvironmentSummaryData::$type`, `EnvironmentOptionData::$type`, `RuleScopeData::$type`,
  `AlertData::$environmentType`, `MaintenanceWindowData::$environmentType`,
  `MaintenanceTargetData::$environmentType`, `ApplicationFormPageData::$types`,
  `EnvironmentFormPageData::$types`, `::$domain`, `::$baseHorizonUrl`, `::$baseEnvironmentName`,
  `WallPageData::$types` (all `types` are `array<int, array{value: string, label: string}>` from
  `EnvironmentType::options()`). `isProduction` and `color` disappear from every Data class.
- Migrations `2026_10_16_000001` to `2026_10_16_000003`; later batches number their
  `2026_10_16_*` migrations from `000004`. The migration test of Task 1.2 inserts old alert rows
  with `unit` and `notified`: Batch 7, which drops those columns, must drop them from
  `oldAlert` in `tests/Feature/Monitoring/EnvironmentTypeMigrationTest.php` too.
- TypeScript: `lib/environments.ts` also exports `typeForName(name): App.Enums.EnvironmentType`
  (suggestion or `'staging'`), `hostOf(url): string | null` and
  `domainOf(environments): string | null`, `followSuggestion<T>(current, suggestion, edited): T`
  and `leavesSuggestion(typed, suggestion): boolean`;
  `composables/useSuggestedHorizonUrl.ts` exports
  `useSuggestedHorizonUrl(url, base, name): { suggestedUrl; urlEdited; onUrlInput }`.
  `EnvironmentForm.vue` gets the model
  `typeEdited` and the boolean prop `typeFollowsName` (replacing `productionEdited` and
  `suggestProduction`); `WizardRow.typeEdited` replaces `productionEdited`;
  `ApplicationWizard.domain` replaces `horizonPath`; `useApplicationWizard()` takes no argument.
  `EnvPill` takes `type` (its `color` and `production` props go), `EnvSwatch` takes `type`.
  `WallFilters` has the model `environmentType` and the prop `types`; `MobileWall` takes
  `typeLabel` instead of `environmentName`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `app/Enums/EnvironmentType.php`

```php
<?php

namespace App\Enums;

enum EnvironmentType: string
{
    case Production = 'production';
    case Preprod = 'preprod';
    case Staging = 'staging';
    case Development = 'development';
    case Testing = 'testing';
    case Demo = 'demo';

    public function label(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Production => __('Production'),
            self::Preprod => __('Pre-production'),
            self::Staging => __('Staging'),
            self::Development => __('Development'),
            self::Testing => __('Testing'),
            self::Demo => __('Demo'),
        };
    }

    public function isProduction(): bool
    {
        return $this === self::Production;
    }

    /**
     * @return array<int, array{value: string, label: string}>
     */
    public static function options(): array
    {
        return array_map(
            fn (self $type) => ['value' => $type->value, 'label' => $type->label()],
            self::cases(),
        );
    }

    public static function suggestFor(string $name): ?self
    {
        $name = strtolower(trim($name));

        if (preg_match('/^pre-production(?:[-._\s]|$)/', $name) === 1) {
            return self::Preprod;
        }

        return match ((string) preg_replace('/[-._\s].*$/s', '', $name)) {
            'production', 'prod', 'prd', 'live' => self::Production,
            'preprod', 'uat' => self::Preprod,
            'staging', 'stage' => self::Staging,
            'develop', 'development', 'dev' => self::Development,
            'test', 'testing', 'qa' => self::Testing,
            'demo' => self::Demo,
            default => null,
        };
    }
}
```

```php
        'develop' => EnvironmentType::Development,

test('rolling back restores the colour, the production flag and the application host', function () {
    $cases = [
        'production' => [Environment::factory()->production(), 'prod', EnvironmentType::Production],
        'preprod' => [Environment::factory()->preprod(), 'preprod', EnvironmentType::Preprod],
        'staging' => [Environment::factory()->staging(), 'staging', EnvironmentType::Staging],
        'develop' => [Environment::factory()->develop(), 'develop', EnvironmentType::Development],
        'demo' => [Environment::factory()->demo(), 'demo', EnvironmentType::Demo],
        'testing' => [Environment::factory()->testing(), 'testing', EnvironmentType::Testing],
    ];
    $environments = [];
    $alerts = [];

    foreach ($cases as $key => [$factory]) {
        $environments[$key] = $factory->for($this->application)->create(
            $key === 'production' ? ['horizon_url' => 'https://billing.example.com/horizon'] : [],
        );
        $alerts[$key] = Alert::factory()->for($environments[$key])->create();
    }

    $empty = Application::factory()->create(['name' => 'Empty']);

    ($this->rollBack)();

    $rows = DB::table('environments')->whereIn('id', array_map(fn (Environment $environment) => $environment->id, $environments))->get()->keyBy('id');

    foreach ($cases as $key => [, $color]) {
        $id = $environments[$key]->id;

        expect($rows[$id]->color)->toBe($color)
            ->and((bool) $rows[$id]->is_production)->toBe($key === 'production')
            ->and(DB::table('alerts')->where('id', $alerts[$key]->id)->value('environment_color'))->toBe($color);
    }

    expect(DB::table('applications')->where('id', $this->application->id)->value('host'))->toBe('billing.example.com')
        ->and(DB::table('applications')->where('id', $empty->id)->value('host'))->toBe('')
        ->and(Schema::hasColumn('environments', 'type'))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(Schema::hasColumn('alerts', 'environment_type'))->toBeFalse();

    ($this->migrate)();

    foreach ($cases as $key => [, , $type]) {
        expect($environments[$key]->fresh()->type)->toBe($type)
            ->and($alerts[$key]->fresh()->environment_type)->toBe($type);
    }
});
```

```php
<?php

namespace Database\Factories;

use App\Enums\EnvironmentType;
use App\Models\Application;
use App\Models\Environment;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\Factory;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * @extends Factory<Environment>
 */
class EnvironmentFactory extends Factory
{
    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    public function definition(): array
    {
        return array_merge(
            $this->typical('production', EnvironmentType::Production),
            [
                'application_id' => Application::factory(),
                'type' => fn (array $attributes) => EnvironmentType::suggestFor((string) $attributes['name']) ?? EnvironmentType::Staging,
            ],
        );
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    private function typical(string $name, EnvironmentType $type): array
    {
        $hasBasicAuth = in_array($type, [EnvironmentType::Production, EnvironmentType::Preprod], true);

        return [
            'name' => $name,
            'type' => $type,
            'horizon_url' => 'https://'.Str::slug($name).'.example.com/horizon',
            'basic_auth_user' => $hasBasicAuth ? 'monitor' : null,
            'basic_auth_password' => $hasBasicAuth ? fake()->password() : null,
            'poll_interval_seconds' => config()->integer('horizon-watch.readings.poll_interval_seconds.default'),
        ];
    }

    public function production(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn () => $this->typical('production', EnvironmentType::Production));
    }

    public function preprod(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn () => $this->typical('preprod', EnvironmentType::Preprod));
    }

    public function staging(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn () => $this->typical('staging', EnvironmentType::Staging));
    }

    public function develop(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn () => $this->typical('develop', EnvironmentType::Development));
    }

    public function demo(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn () => $this->typical('demo', EnvironmentType::Demo));
    }

    public function workerBatch(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn () => $this->typical('worker-batch', EnvironmentType::Staging));
    }

    public function testing(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn () => $this->typical('testing', EnvironmentType::Testing));
    }
}
```

```php
function horizonUrlErrors(string $url): array

    return Validator::make(['horizonUrl' => $url], ['horizonUrl' => EnvironmentFormData::horizonUrlRules()])
        ->errors()
        ->get('horizonUrl');
}

test('a horizon url with a query string or a fragment is refused', function (string $url) {
    expect(horizonUrlErrors($url))->toBe(['The Horizon URL cannot have a query string or a fragment.']);
})->with([
    'query' => 'https://shop.example.com/horizon?x=1',
    'fragment' => 'https://shop.example.com/horizon#/dashboard',
    'both' => 'https://shop.example.com/horizon/?x=1#top',
    'empty query' => 'https://shop.example.com/horizon?',
    'empty fragment' => 'https://shop.example.com/horizon#',
]);

test('a plain horizon url passes', function (string $url) {
    expect(horizonUrlErrors($url))->toBe([]);
})->with([
    'dashboard' => 'https://shop.example.com/horizon',
    'with a port and a slash' => 'http://horizon.internal:8080/horizon/',
]);

test('the credentials are judged first, and one message is enough', function () {
    expect(horizonUrlErrors('https://monitor:secret@shop.example.com/horizon?x=1'))
        ->toBe(['Put the credentials in the basic-auth fields, not in the Horizon URL.']);
});

test('an address on a network the panel never calls is refused', function (string $url) {
    expect(horizonUrlErrors($url))->toBe(['This address points to a network the panel does not call.']);
})->with([
    'the metadata address' => 'http://169.254.169.254/horizon',
    'the metadata name' => 'http://metadata.google.internal/horizon',
]);

test('a mapped metadata address is refused too', function () {
    expect(horizonUrlErrors('http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/horizon'))
        ->toContain('This address points to a network the panel does not call.');
});

test('a private address is refused only when private networks are blocked', function (bool $blocked) {
    config(['horizon-watch.block_private_networks' => $blocked]);

    expect(horizonUrlErrors('http://10.0.0.5/horizon'))
        ->toBe($blocked ? ['This address points to a network the panel does not call.'] : []);
})->with([true, false]);

test('a host name is never resolved while validating', function () {
    $this->mock(Resolver::class)->shouldNotReceive('resolve');

    expect(horizonUrlErrors('https://unresolvable.invalid/horizon'))->toBe([]);
});

test('an address that is not http gets the url message only', function () {
    expect(horizonUrlErrors('ftp://shop.example.com/horizon'))->toHaveCount(1);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the normaliser** `app/Support/HorizonUrl.php`

```php
<?php

namespace App\Support;

final class HorizonUrl
{
    private const string AUTHORITY = '#^([a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*)://((?:[^/?\#@]*@)?)([^/?\#]*)#i';

    private const string API_SUFFIX = '#^([a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://[^/?\#]+/[^?\#]*?[^/?\#])/api(?:/[^?\#]*)?$#i';

    public static function normalize(string $url): string
    {
        $url = (string) preg_replace_callback(
            self::AUTHORITY,
            fn (array $parts): string => strtolower($parts[1]).'://'.$parts[2].strtolower($parts[3]),
            trim($url),
        );

        if (preg_match('/[?#]/', $url) === 1) {
            return $url;
        }

        return rtrim((string) preg_replace(self::API_SUFFIX, '$1', rtrim($url, '/')), '/');
    }

    public static function host(string $url): ?string
    {
        $host = parse_url(trim($url), PHP_URL_HOST);

        return is_string($host) && $host !== '' ? strtolower($host) : null;
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the outbound rule** `app/Rules/OutboundUrl.php`

```php
<?php

namespace App\Rules;

use App\Enums\ReadingError;
use App\Externals\Http\Dns\Resolver;
use App\Externals\Http\SafeUrlGuard;
use App\Externals\Http\UrlRefused;
use Closure;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Validation\ValidationRule;
use Illuminate\Translation\PotentiallyTranslatedString;

class OutboundUrl implements ValidationRule
{
    public static function carriesCredentials(string $url): bool
    {
        return preg_match('#^[^:/?\#]*://[^/?\#]*@#', trim($url)) === 1;
    }

    public static function carriesQueryOrFragment(string $url): bool
    {
        return str_contains($url, '?') || str_contains($url, '#');
    }

    /**
     * @param  Closure(string, ?string=): PotentiallyTranslatedString  $fail
     */
    public function validate(string $attribute, mixed $value, Closure $fail): void
    {
        if (! is_string($value)) {
            return;
        }

        $url = trim($value);

        if (preg_match('#^https?://#i', $url) !== 1) {
            return;
        }

        if (self::carriesCredentials($url)) {
            $fail($this->credentialsMessage());

            return;
        }

        if (self::carriesQueryOrFragment($url)) {
            $fail($this->queryMessage());

            return;
        }

        if ($this->blocked($url)) {
            $fail($this->blockedMessage());
        }
    }

    protected function credentialsMessage(): string
    {
        return __('Put the credentials in the basic-auth fields, not in the Horizon URL.');
    }

    protected function queryMessage(): string
    {
        return __('The Horizon URL cannot have a query string or a fragment.');
    }

    protected function blockedMessage(): string
    {
        return __('This address points to a network the panel does not call.');
    }

    private function blocked(string $url): bool
    {
        $guard = new SafeUrlGuard(
            new class implements Resolver
            {
                public function resolve(string $host): array
                {
                    return filter_var($host, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP) === false ? [] : [$host];
                }
            },
            config()->boolean('horizon-watch.block_private_networks', false),
        );

        try {
            $guard->check($url);
        } catch (UrlRefused $exception) {
            return $exception->reason === ReadingError::Blocked;
        }

        return false;
    }
}
```

```php
<?php

namespace App\Queries;

use App\Data\Applications\ApplicationFormData;
use App\Data\Applications\EnvironmentFormData;
use App\Data\Pages\EnvironmentFormPageData;
use App\Enums\EnvironmentType;

    public function handle(Application $application): EnvironmentFormPageData
    {

        return new EnvironmentFormPageData(
            environment: null,
            application: ApplicationFormData::from($application),
            types: EnvironmentType::options(),
            hasPassword: false,
            applicationSlug: $application->slug,
            domain: $primary === null ? null : HorizonUrl::host($primary->horizon_url),
            baseHorizonUrl: $primary === null ? null : EnvironmentFormData::withoutUserinfo($primary->horizon_url),
            baseEnvironmentName: $primary?->name,
        );
    }
}
```

```php
    /**
     * @param  Collection<int, Environment>  $environments
     */
    private function toApplicationData(Application $application, Collection $environments): ApplicationData
    {
        $primary = Application::primaryEnvironment($environments->where('application_id', $application->id));

        return new ApplicationData(
            id: $application->slug,
            name: $application->name,
            domain: $primary === null ? null : HorizonUrl::host($primary->horizon_url),
        );
    }
```

```ts
    ['production', 'production'],
```

```ts
]);

export function suggestType(name: string): App.Enums.EnvironmentType | null {
    const normalized = name.trim().toLowerCase();

    if (/^pre-production(?:[-._\s]|$)/.test(normalized)) {
        return 'preprod';
    }

    return SUGGESTIONS.get(normalized.split(/[-._\s]/, 1)[0]) ?? null;
}

export function typeForName(name: string): App.Enums.EnvironmentType {
    return suggestType(name) ?? 'staging';
}

export function isProductionType(
    type: App.Enums.EnvironmentType | null | undefined,
): boolean {
    return type === 'production';
}

function parsed(url: string): URL | null {
    try {
        const candidate = new URL(url.trim());

        return /^https?:$/.test(candidate.protocol) && candidate.hostname !== ''
            ? candidate
            : null;
    } catch {
        return null;
    }
}

export function hostOf(url: string): string | null {
    return parsed(url)?.hostname ?? null;
}

export function domainOf(
    environments: ReadonlyArray<{
        type: App.Enums.EnvironmentType;
        horizonUrl: string;
    }>,
): string | null {
    const primary =
        environments.find((environment) =>
            isProductionType(environment.type),
        ) ?? environments[0];

    return primary === undefined ? null : hostOf(primary.horizonUrl);
}

export function suggestHorizonUrl(
    baseUrl: string,
    baseName: string,
    name: string,
): string {
    const base = parsed(baseUrl);
    const environment = name.trim().toLowerCase();

    if (base === null || environment === '') {
        return '';
    }

    const label = baseName.trim().toLowerCase();
    const baseHost =
        label !== '' && base.hostname.startsWith(`${label}.`)
            ? base.hostname.slice(label.length + 1)
            : base.hostname;
    const host = isProductionType(suggestType(environment))
        ? baseHost
        : `${environment}.${baseHost}`;
    const port = base.port === '' ? '' : `:${base.port}`;

    return `${base.protocol}//${host}${port}${dashboardPath(base.pathname)}`;
}

/**
 * The path HorizonUrl::normalize() would store: no trailing slash, and no trailing `/api…`
 * part when at least one segment comes before it (a Horizon served at `/api` keeps it).
 */
function dashboardPath(pathname: string): string {
    return pathname
        .replace(/\/+$/, '')
        .replace(/^(\/.*?[^/])\/api(?:\/.*)?$/, '$1');
}
```

The three new `suggestHorizonUrl` rows are a Review Focus pin (see `00-header.md`): a first row
pasted from Horizon's API or with capitals must suggest the dashboard path the server will store,
otherwise the wizard's step 3 and the blur connection test of Add environment test
`…/horizon/api/stats/api/…` and report a 404 before anything is saved.

```ts
}
```

Append to `resources/js/lib/environments.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * What a field prefilled with a suggestion holds: the suggestion, until the user edits the field
 * by hand. The wizard's further URL rows, the Add environment URL and the type that follows the
 * name all go through this one rule.
 */
export function followSuggestion<T>(
    current: T,
    suggestion: T,
    edited: boolean,
): T {
    return edited ? current : suggestion;
}

/**
 * Whether what the user just typed leaves the suggestion. Typing the suggestion back makes the
 * field follow it again.
 */
export function leavesSuggestion(typed: string, suggestion: string): boolean {
    return typed !== suggestion;
}
```

`resources/js/composables/useSuggestedHorizonUrl.ts`:

```ts
import type { ComputedRef, Ref } from 'vue';
import { computed, ref, watchEffect } from 'vue';
import {
    followSuggestion,
    leavesSuggestion,
    suggestHorizonUrl,
} from '@/lib/environments';

export type HorizonUrlBase = { horizonUrl: string; name: string };

export type SuggestedHorizonUrl = {
    suggestedUrl: ComputedRef<string>;
    urlEdited: Ref<boolean>;
    onUrlInput: () => void;
};

/**
 * A Horizon URL field prefilled with the URL suggested from a base environment for the name
 * being typed (the wizard's rule, through `suggestHorizonUrl`). It follows the suggestion until
 * the user types another URL; `onUrlInput` runs on every input of the field.
 */
export function useSuggestedHorizonUrl(
    url: Ref<string>,
    base: () => HorizonUrlBase | null,
    name: () => string,
): SuggestedHorizonUrl {
    const urlEdited = ref(false);

    const suggestedUrl = computed(() => {
        const from = base();

        return from === null
            ? ''
            : suggestHorizonUrl(from.horizonUrl, from.name, name());
    });

    watchEffect(() => {
        url.value = followSuggestion(
            url.value,
            suggestedUrl.value,
            urlEdited.value,
        );
    });

    const onUrlInput = (): void => {
        urlEdited.value = leavesSuggestion(url.value, suggestedUrl.value);
    };

    return { suggestedUrl, urlEdited, onUrlInput };
}
```

```vue
const model = defineModel<App.Data.Applications.EnvironmentFormData>({

    prefix?: string;
    hasPassword?: boolean;
    compact?: boolean;
    typeFollowsName?: boolean;
}>();

    urlInput: [];
}>();

const fieldId = (field: string) => `${prefix}${field}`.replace(/\./g, '-');

const errorOf = (field: string) => errors[`${prefix}${field}`];

const credentialsInClear = computed(
    () =>
        /^\s*http:\/\//i.test(model.value.horizonUrl ?? '') &&
        !!model.value.basicAuthUser?.trim(),
);

const toggleAuth = () => {
    auth.value = !auth.value;

    if (!auth.value) {
        model.value.basicAuthUser = null;
        model.value.basicAuthPassword = null;
    }
};

watch(
    () => model.value.name,
    (name) => {
        if (typeFollowsName) {
            model.value.type = followSuggestion(
                model.value.type,
                typeForName(name),
                typeEdited.value,
            );
        }
    },
);

const [DefineName, NameField] = createReusableTemplate();
const [DefineType, TypeField] = createReusableTemplate();
const [DefineUrl, UrlField] = createReusableTemplate();
const [DefineCredentials, CredentialFields] = createReusableTemplate();
const [DefineInterval, IntervalField] = createReusableTemplate();
const [DefineCollect, CollectField] = createReusableTemplate();
</script>
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Head, Link, useForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3';

});

    page: App.Data.Pages.EnvironmentFormPageData;
}>();

const form = useForm<{
    environment: App.Data.Applications.EnvironmentFormData;
}>({
    environment: {
        name: '',
        type: typeForName(''),
        horizonUrl: '',
        basicAuthUser: null,
        basicAuthPassword: null,
        pollIntervalSeconds: 15,
        pollingEnabled: true,
    },
});

const typeEdited = ref(false);

    }),
    () =>
        page.baseHorizonUrl === null
            ? null
            : {

                  name: page.baseEnvironmentName ?? '',
              },
    () => form.environment.name,
);

}));

);
```

```ts
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vite-plus/test';
import { computed, nextTick, reactive } from 'vue';
import { useApplicationWizard } from '@/composables/useApplicationWizard';

const inertia = vi.hoisted(() => ({
    post: vi.fn(),
    clearErrors: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock('@inertiajs/vue3', () => ({
    useForm: <T extends object>(data: T) =>
        reactive({
            ...data,
            errors: {} as Record<string, string>,
            post: inertia.post,
            clearErrors: inertia.clearErrors,
        }),
}));

vi.mock('@/composables/useTeamSlug', () => ({
    useTeamSlug: () => computed(() => 'acme'),
}));

vi.mock('@/routes/applications', () => ({
    store: (team: string) => ({ url: `/${team}/applications`, method: 'post' }),
}));

const BASE_URL = 'https://shop.example.com/horizon';

const reachable = (yes: boolean) =>
    ({
        state: 'done',
        result: {
            reachable: yes,
            horizonStatus: yes ? 'running' : null,
            masterCount: yes ? 1 : null,
            latencyMs: 40,
            error: yes ? null : 'unreachable',
            problem: null,
            suggestedUrl: null,
            credentialsInClear: false,
        },
    }) as const;

async function wizardFor(baseUrl = BASE_URL) {
    const wizard = useApplicationWizard();

    wizard.form.application.name = 'Billing';
    wizard.form.environments[0].horizonUrl = baseUrl;
    await nextTick();

    return wizard;
}

beforeEach(() => {
    inertia.post.mockReset();
    inertia.clearErrors.mockReset();
});

describe('useApplicationWizard', () => {
    it('starts with a production environment whose URL is typed by hand', () => {
        const { form, rows } = useApplicationWizard();

        expect(form.application).toEqual({ name: '' });
        expect(form.environments).toEqual([
            {
                name: 'production',
                type: 'production',
                horizonUrl: '',
                basicAuthUser: null,
                basicAuthPassword: null,
                pollIntervalSeconds: 15,
                pollingEnabled: true,
            },
        ]);
        expect(rows.value[0]).toMatchObject({
            urlEdited: false,
            typeEdited: false,
        });
    });

    it('suggests the next usual environment with its type', async () => {
        const { form, addEnvironment } = await wizardFor();

        addEnvironment();
        addEnvironment();
        addEnvironment();

        ).toEqual([
            ['production', 'production'],
            ['staging', 'staging'],
            ['preprod', 'preprod'],
            ['develop', 'development'],
        ]);
    });

    it('falls back to an unnamed staging environment once the usual names are taken', () => {
        const { form, addEnvironment } = useApplicationWizard();

        for (let added = 0; added < 6; added++) {
            addEnvironment();
        }

        expect(
            form.environments.slice(4).map(({ name, type }) => [name, type]),
        ).toEqual([
            ['demo', 'demo'],
            ['testing', 'testing'],
            ['', 'staging'],
        ]);
    });

    it('derives each further Horizon URL from the first row', async () => {
        const { form, addEnvironment } = await wizardFor();

        addEnvironment();
        await nextTick();

        expect(form.environments.map((env) => env.horizonUrl)).toEqual([
            'https://shop.example.com/horizon',
            'https://staging.shop.example.com/horizon',
        ]);

        form.environments[0].horizonUrl =
            'https://production.shop.example.com/ops/horizon/';
        await nextTick();

        expect(form.environments[1].horizonUrl).toBe(
            'https://staging.shop.example.com/ops/horizon',
        );

        form.environments[1].name = 'qa';
        await nextTick();

        expect(form.environments[1].horizonUrl).toBe(
            'https://qa.shop.example.com/ops/horizon',
        );
        expect(form.environments[0].horizonUrl).toBe(
            'https://production.shop.example.com/ops/horizon/',
        );
    });

    it('stops suggesting once a further URL is edited by hand', async () => {
        const { form, rows, onUrlInput, addEnvironment } = await wizardFor();

        addEnvironment();
        await nextTick();

        form.environments[1].horizonUrl = 'https://horizon.example.net';

        form.environments[0].horizonUrl = 'https://example.org/horizon';

        wizard.form.environments[0].horizonUrl = BASE_URL;
        wizard.addEnvironment();
        await nextTick();

        expect(wizard.environmentsFilled.value).toBe(true);

        form.environments[1].type = 'production';

        expect(domain.value).toBe('live.example.net');
    });

    it('tests again on the last step only what changed since the last test', async () => {
        const { form, rows, step, addEnvironment } = await wizardFor();

        addEnvironment();
        step.value = 3;
        await nextTick();

        expect(rows.value.every((row) => row.autoTest)).toBe(true);

        rows.value[0].outcome = reachable(true);
        rows.value[1].outcome = { state: 'testing' };
        step.value = 2;
        await nextTick();

        form.environments[0].basicAuthUser = 'ops';
        step.value = 3;
        await nextTick();

        expect(rows.value[0].outcome).toEqual({ state: 'idle' });
        expect(rows.value[0].autoTest).toBe(true);
        expect(rows.value[1].outcome).toEqual({ state: 'idle' });
        expect(rows.value[1].autoTest).toBe(false);

        rows.value[0].outcome = reachable(true);
        step.value = 2;
        await nextTick();
        step.value = 3;
        await nextTick();

        expect(rows.value[0].outcome).toEqual(reachable(true));
    });

    it('runs the connection test again only where it failed', async () => {
        const { rows, rememberTest, testAgain, addEnvironment, testing } =
            await wizardFor();

        addEnvironment();
        const first = { run: vi.fn(async () => {}) };
        const second = { run: vi.fn(async () => {}) };

        rememberTest(rows.value[0].key, first);
        rememberTest(rows.value[1].key, second);
        rows.value[0].outcome = reachable(true);
        rows.value[1].outcome = reachable(false);

        await testAgain();

        expect(first.run).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
        expect(second.run).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();

        rememberTest(rows.value[1].key, null);
        await testAgain();

        expect(second.run).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();

        rows.value[1].outcome = { state: 'testing' };

        expect(testing.value).toBe(true);
    });

    it('posts to the team and returns to the step with the first error', async () => {
        const { submit, step, rows, addEnvironment } = await wizardFor();

        addEnvironment();
        step.value = 3;
        submit();

        expect(inertia.post).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
            '/acme/applications',
            expect.any(Object),
        );

        const { onError } = inertia.post.mock.calls[0][1] as {

        };

        onError({ 'environments.1.basicAuthPassword': 'Required.' });

        expect(step.value).toBe(2);
        expect(rows.value.map((row) => row.auth)).toEqual([false, true]);

        onError({ 'application.name': 'Taken.', 'environments.0.name': 'x' });

        expect(step.value).toBe(1);

        expect(step.value).toBe(3);

    it('lists the errors no field shows', async () => {

            'application.name': 'Required.',
            'environments.0.horizonUrl': 'Invalid.',
            limit: 'Too many environments.',
        });

        expect(unplacedErrors.value).toEqual(['Too many environments.']);
    });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `resources/js/composables/useApplicationWizard.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import type { InertiaForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3';
import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3';
import type { ComputedRef, Ref } from 'vue';
import { computed, ref, watch, watchEffect } from 'vue';
import type { ConnectionOutcome } from '@/components/monitoring/applications/ConnectionTest.vue';
import { useTeamSlug } from '@/composables/useTeamSlug';
import {
    domainOf,
    followSuggestion,
    leavesSuggestion,
    suggestHorizonUrl,
    typeForName,
} from '@/lib/environments';
import { store } from '@/routes/applications';

export type WizardRow = {
    key: number;
    auth: boolean;
    urlEdited: boolean;
    typeEdited: boolean;
    outcome: ConnectionOutcome;
    testedSignature: string;
    autoTest: boolean;
};

type ConnectionTester = { run: () => Promise<void> };

type WizardForm = {
    application: App.Data.Applications.ApplicationFormData;
    environments: App.Data.Applications.EnvironmentFormData[];
};

export type ApplicationWizard = {
    step: Ref<number>;
    form: InertiaForm<WizardForm>;
    rows: Ref<WizardRow[]>;
    errors: ComputedRef<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
    unplacedErrors: ComputedRef<string[]>;
    applicationFilled: ComputedRef<boolean>;
    environmentsFilled: ComputedRef<boolean>;
    domain: ComputedRef<string | null>;
    testing: ComputedRef<boolean>;
    addEnvironment: () => void;
    removeEnvironment: (index: number) => void;
    onUrlInput: (index: number) => void;
    testPayload: (
        environment: App.Data.Applications.EnvironmentFormData,
    ) => App.Data.Applications.TestConnectionData;
    rememberTest: (key: number, instance: unknown) => void;
    testAgain: () => Promise<void>;
    submit: () => void;
};

const SUGGESTED_NAMES = [
    'production',
    'staging',
    'preprod',
    'develop',
    'demo',
    'testing',
];

export function useApplicationWizard(): ApplicationWizard {
    const slug = useTeamSlug();

    const step = ref(1);

    let nextKey = 0;

    const blankEnvironment = (
        taken: string[],
    ): App.Data.Applications.EnvironmentFormData => {
        const name =
            SUGGESTED_NAMES.find((candidate) => !taken.includes(candidate)) ??
            '';

        return {
            name,
            type: typeForName(name),
            horizonUrl: '',
            basicAuthUser: null,
            basicAuthPassword: null,
            pollIntervalSeconds: 15,
            pollingEnabled: true,
        };
    };

    const blankRow = (): WizardRow => ({
        key: nextKey++,
        auth: false,
        urlEdited: false,
        typeEdited: false,
        outcome: { state: 'idle' },
        testedSignature: '',
        autoTest: true,
    });

    const form = useForm<WizardForm>({
        application: { name: '' },
        environments: [blankEnvironment([])],
    });

    const rows = ref<WizardRow[]>([blankRow()]);

    const errors = computed(
        () => form.errors as Record<string, string | undefined>,
    );

    const suggestedUrl = (index: number): string => {
        const base = form.environments[0];
        const environment = form.environments[index];

        return index === 0 || base === undefined || environment === undefined
            ? ''
            : suggestHorizonUrl(base.horizonUrl, base.name, environment.name);
    };

    watchEffect(() => {
        form.environments.forEach((environment, index) => {
            if (index > 0) {
                environment.horizonUrl = followSuggestion(
                    environment.horizonUrl,
                    suggestedUrl(index),
                    rows.value[index]?.urlEdited ?? false,
                );
            }
        });
    });

    const onUrlInput = (index: number): void => {
        if (index > 0) {
            rows.value[index].urlEdited = leavesSuggestion(
                form.environments[index].horizonUrl,
                suggestedUrl(index),
            );
        }
    };

    const applicationFilled = computed(
        () => form.application.name.trim() !== '',
    );

    const environmentsFilled = computed(
        () =>
            form.environments.length > 0 &&
            form.environments.every(
                (environment) =>
                    environment.name.trim() !== '' &&
                    environment.horizonUrl.trim() !== '',
            ),
    );

    const domain = computed(() => domainOf(form.environments));

    const addEnvironment = (): void => {
        form.environments.push(
            blankEnvironment(
                form.environments.map((environment) => environment.name.trim()),
            ),
        );
        rows.value.push(blankRow());
    };

    const removeEnvironment = (index: number): void => {
        form.environments.splice(index, 1);
        rows.value.splice(index, 1);
        form.clearErrors();
    };

    const testPayload = (
        environment: App.Data.Applications.EnvironmentFormData,
    ): App.Data.Applications.TestConnectionData => ({
        horizonUrl: environment.horizonUrl,
        basicAuthUser: environment.basicAuthUser,
        basicAuthPassword: environment.basicAuthPassword,
    });

    const signatureOf = (
        environment: App.Data.Applications.EnvironmentFormData,
    ) => JSON.stringify(testPayload(environment));

    watch(step, (current) => {
        if (current !== 3) {
            return;
        }

        form.environments.forEach((environment, index) => {
            const row = rows.value[index];
            const signature = signatureOf(environment);

            if (row.testedSignature !== signature) {
                row.outcome = { state: 'idle' };
                row.testedSignature = signature;
                row.autoTest = true;
            } else if (row.outcome.state === 'testing') {
                row.outcome = { state: 'idle' };
                row.autoTest = false;
            }
        });
    });

    const tests = new Map<number, ConnectionTester>();

    const rememberTest = (key: number, instance: unknown): void => {
        if (instance) {
            tests.set(key, instance as ConnectionTester);
        } else {
            tests.delete(key);
        }
    };

    const reachable = (outcome: ConnectionOutcome): boolean =>
        outcome.state === 'done' && outcome.result.reachable;

    const testAgain = async (): Promise<void> => {
        for (const row of rows.value.slice()) {
            if (!reachable(row.outcome)) {
                await tests.get(row.key)?.run();
            }
        }
    };

    const testing = computed(() =>
        rows.value.some((row) => row.outcome.state === 'testing'),
    );

    const stepOf = (keys: string[]): number => {
        if (keys.some((key) => key.startsWith('application'))) {
            return 1;
        }

        return keys.some((key) => key.startsWith('environments')) ? 2 : 3;
    };

    const unplacedErrors = computed(() =>
        Object.entries(errors.value)
            .filter(
                ([key]) =>
                    !key.startsWith('application') &&
                    !key.startsWith('environments'),
            )
            .map(([, message]) => message)
            .filter((message): message is string => Boolean(message)),
    );

    const submit = (): void => {
        form.post(store(slug.value).url, {
            onError: (bag) => {
                const keys = Object.keys(bag);

                rows.value.forEach((row, index) => {
                    if (
                        keys.some((key) =>
                            key.startsWith(`environments.${index}.basicAuth`),
                        )
                    ) {
                        row.auth = true;
                    }
                });

                step.value = stepOf(keys);
            },
        });
    };

    return {
        step,
        form,
        rows,
        errors,
        unplacedErrors,
        applicationFilled,
        environmentsFilled,
        domain,
        testing,
        addEnvironment,
        removeEnvironment,
        onUrlInput,
        testPayload,
        rememberTest,
        testAgain,
        submit,
    };
}
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, useId } from 'vue';
import SegmentedControl from '@/components/nocturne/SegmentedControl.vue';
import { envTypeColor } from '@/lib/monitoring';

const { environments, problemCount, types } = defineProps<{
    environments: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData[];
    problemCount: number;
    types: App.Data.Pages.WallPageData['types'];
}>();

const filter = defineModel<'all' | 'problems'>('filter', { required: true });
const environmentType = defineModel<App.Enums.EnvironmentType | ''>(
    'environmentType',
    { required: true },
);
const search = defineModel<string>('search', { required: true });

const id = useId();

const chips = computed(() =>
    types
        .map((option) => {
            const type = option.value as App.Enums.EnvironmentType;

            return {
                type,
                label: option.label,
                color: envTypeColor(type),
                count: environments.filter(
                    (environment) => environment.type === type,
                ).length,
            };
        })
        .filter((chip) => chip.count > 0),
);
</script>
```

```bash
next to an application. The wizard asks for the first URL and suggests the

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

## Batch 2: One environment state, one set of KPIs, the judged numbers

Goal: every surface derives an environment's state from one helper set with one precedence
(not visible > collection paused > reading error > stale > no reading yet > Horizon status), one
wording and one tone per state; a paused collection is calm everywhere and is left out of the
healthy and needs-attention counts on the server; the wall KPIs are defined once and shared by
desktop and mobile; "needs attention" is the one term for the filter, the KPI, the badge and the
empty states; and every figure is coloured only by its own rule, with the rule severity, showing
the number the rule judges (failed jobs in the last hour) and Horizon's window count as a neutral
note. Spec themes covered: **3** (environment state), **4** (wall KPIs and needs attention),
**5** (show the number the product judges).

Assumptions from Batch 1 (already merged when this batch runs):

- `EnvironmentData` has `public EnvironmentType $type` instead of `color` and `isProduction`;
  `EnvPill` takes `:type="environment.type"`; `envColor()` is gone and `envTypeColor(type)`
  exists in `lib/monitoring.ts`. Every Vue block below shows those lines as Batch 1 left them. If
  Batch 1 named an `EnvPill`/`EnvSwatch` prop differently, keep Batch 1's line and apply only the
  changes this batch describes around it.
- Factory states `->production()` and `->staging()` still exist on `EnvironmentFactory`.
- Batch 1 Task 1.10 changed the wall filters: `WallFilters.vue` destructures
  `{ environments, problemCount, types }` (prop `types: App.Data.Pages.WallPageData['types']`)
  and has the model `environmentType` (`App.Enums.EnvironmentType | ''`) instead of
  `environmentName`; `Wall.vue` holds `environmentType` and `typeLabel` refs and passes
  `v-model:environment-type="environmentType"` and `:types="page.types"` to `WallFilters` and
  `:type-label="typeLabel"` to `MobileWall`; `MobileWall.vue` takes the prop `typeLabel: string`
  instead of `environmentName`. Every block below is written against those names.

Line numbers: every line number in this part is the line in the file as it is on `release/1.0`
before Batch 1. Where Batch 1 edits the same file (`EnvironmentData.php`,
`ConfiguredMonitoringRepository.php`, `WallQuery.php`, `WallTest.php`, `ApplicationPagesTest.php`,
`lib/monitoring.ts`, `monitoring.test.ts`, `Wall.vue`, `WallFilters.vue`, `MobileWall.vue`,
`environments/Show.vue`, `EnvironmentTile.vue`, `EnvironmentMobile.vue`, `ApplicationGroup.vue`,
`ApplicationList.vue`, `EnvironmentCard.vue`, `EnvironmentComparison.vue`,
`ApplicationSection.vue`), the numbers can be off by a few lines (by eleven in
`environments/Show.vue` below line 73, where Batch 1 deletes `mastersPath`):
locate the block by the code quoted with it, which Batch 1 does not change unless stated.

Not in this batch (later batches own them): formatter consolidation (`formatWait`, `formatAge`,
`formatElapsed`, theme 6, Batch 3), the `anomaly` to `alert` renames including
`WallKpisData::$openAnomalies` and `AnomalyList` (theme 7, Batch 4), delivery-error sentence keys
(theme 13, Batch 4), `EnvironmentComparison` removal and the new `EnvironmentCard` stats
(theme 10, Batch 5), `MetricCard` replacing `KpiCard`/`MetricTile` (theme 15, Batch 6), server
`worstStatus` replacing the TypeScript `SEVERITY` copy (theme 17, Batch 7).

Decisions taken where the spec leaves a detail open (one line each, repeated in the task that
applies them):

- "Not persisted to `environment_states`": a paused collection is a display state, not a new
  `EnvironmentStatus` case; `PollEnvironment` already skips disabled environments
  (`PollEnvironmentTest` dataset `paused`), so nothing is stored.
- A reading error reads "unreachable" (short chip text, `--st-down`); the reason
  (`readingErrorLabel`) is the explanation in the banner, the freshness line and the connection
  test.
- "No reading yet" is the one wording of the waiting state; "waiting for the first reading"
  goes.
- `Healthy N / M`: `M` is the environments the wall judges (collection on, with a status).
  Pending and Failed KPIs, and the wall's "12/min now" figure (`WallPageData::$jobsPerMinute`),
  sum the judged environments only, so a paused collection's last reading does not inflate live
  totals (the throughput chart beside "12/min now" has no new points from a paused collection
  either).
- The KPI and the application-list counts come from the server (`environmentsNeedingAttention`,
  `attentionCount`). The client applies the same rule (`needsAttention`) to filter the wall list
  and to count the badge of each wall group, because the wall groups are built on the client.
- The internal wall filter value stays `'problems'` (URLs keep `?filter=problems`); only the label
  changes.
- Open alerts KPI tone: the worst severity among open alerts; Healthy and Pending are neutral (no
  rule of their own); the Workers tile is neutral (no rule judges the process count).
- A paused collection also sorts with the calm rows (`EnvironmentData::severity()`) and is left out
  of the application page's worst status.
- Queue contributor flags are `waitOverThreshold` (`queue.max_wait`) and `withoutWorkers`
  (`workers.missing`), set only while the rule is enabled and the last reading is not down; the
  per-queue pending check is dropped because `queue.pending` is a total across all queues.
- Theme 5's "application cards" figure: `EnvironmentComparison` (the application page table)
  shows Failed · last hour now; Batch 5 moves it into `EnvironmentCard` when it deletes
  `EnvironmentComparison` (theme 10 already lists "Failed (last hour)").
- "Open alerts" keeps its Italian text "Aperti" (alert vocabulary belongs to Batch 4).
- The client "stale" display state follows the server status (`status === 'stale'`), not the raw
  `stale` flag: the server keeps a stale environment last known down as `inactive`/`unreachable`
  (`ConfiguredMonitoringRepositoryTest` "a stale environment last known down stays down"), and the
  chip, the sort and the counts must agree with it. The freshness line still says "Not updated".
- `statusLabel('paused')` becomes "Horizon paused" everywhere `statusLabel` is used, the node card
  included (a node is a Horizon master supervisor, so the wording is still true there).
- Throughput carries its unit on the value as `` `${jobsPerMinute}/min` ``: `/min` is a unit
  symbol, the same in both languages, so it gets no translation key (Batch 5 writes the
  application cards the same way). The label is "Throughput" on desktop and mobile; `Jobs/min`
  goes. The same form holds on every throughput surface: the wall's "now" line reads
  `12/min now` (`:value now`), both throughput charts (wall and environment page) summarise as
  `:range, peak :value` with `value` = `` `${peak}/min` `` and describe each point as
  `` `${value}/min` ``, the environment chart's caption is "Throughput", and the application
  table's column is "Throughput" with `` `${jobsPerMinute}/min` `` cells. The mobile wall shows no
  throughput figure (it drops the chart and its "now" line, as mobile may drop figures), so it
  has nothing to redefine; on mobile, throughput is the environment page's Throughput tile. The
  keys `jobs/min`, `:count jobs/min`, `:count jobs/min now` and `:range, peak :count jobs/min`
  go, and a lasting source test (`StateAndNumbersTest`) keeps `jobs/min` out of the front end.
- Lasting checks of this batch's rules live in `tests/Feature/StateAndNumbersTest.php` (source
  assertions in the style Batch 5 uses for `PagesAndFormsTest`), created in Task 2.8 and extended
  in Tasks 2.9 and 2.10, so a later edit cannot quietly bring back a removed pattern.
- `failedLabel` (`lib/failedWindow.ts`) is deleted: once every Failed figure is the last hour,
  nothing calls it, and its four keys go with it. Batch 3's one unit fragment for failed-window
  labels then applies to `failedWindowShort` alone (and to the `Horizon: :count, :window` note
  through `failedWindowNote`).
- The failed-window note is computed over the judged environments (the ones `failedInWindow`
  sums), falling back to every environment when none is judged, so a paused collection with
  another window does not make the note "each environment over its own window".

Commits: all tasks of this batch are committed together at Task 2.12. The front-end type check
(`vue-tsc`) is expected to fail between Task 2.4 and Task 2.10 while consumers are being moved;
only PHP tests and Vitest are run in between.

`app/Enums/AlertSeverity.php`, add inside the enum after the cases:

```php
    /**
     * @param  array<int, self>  $severities
     */
    public static function worstOf(array $severities): ?self
    {
        if (in_array(self::Critical, $severities, true)) {
            return self::Critical;
        }

        return $severities === [] ? null : self::Warning;
    }
```

`app/Data/Monitoring/EnvironmentData.php`, replace `severity()` (lines 54-59) with the block
below, which adds the three judgement methods. A paused collection sorts like an environment
without a status.

```php
    public function severity(): int
    {
        return $this->status === null || ! $this->pollingEnabled
            ? 2 * EnvironmentStatus::Degraded->severity() + 1
            : 2 * $this->status->severity();
    }

    public function isJudged(): bool
    {
        return $this->watched && $this->pollingEnabled && $this->status !== null;
    }

    public function isHealthy(): bool
    {
        return $this->isJudged() && $this->status?->isHealthy() === true;
    }

    public function needsAttention(): bool
    {
        return $this->isJudged() && $this->status?->isHealthy() === false;
    }
```

```php
    public function queues(Team $team, string $environmentId): array
    {
        $environment = $this->findEnvironment($team, $environmentId);
        $state = $environment ? $this->stateOf($environment) : null;

        if ($state === null) {
            return [];
        }

        $rules = $this->effectiveRules->forEnvironment($environment);
        $measured = ! $state->status->isDown();
        $wait = $rules->for(AlertRuleMetric::QueueMaxWait);
        $workers = $rules->for(AlertRuleMetric::WorkersMissing);

        return array_map(fn (array $queue) => new QueueData(
            name: $queue['name'],
            supervisor: $queue['supervisor'],
            workers: $queue['workers'],
            pending: $queue['pending'],
            waitSeconds: $queue['waitSeconds'],
            runtimeSeconds: $queue['runtimeSeconds'] === null ? null : (float) $queue['runtimeSeconds'],
            waitOverThreshold: $measured && $wait->enabled && $queue['waitSeconds'] > $wait->threshold,
            withoutWorkers: $measured && $workers->enabled && $queue['workers'] === 0 && $queue['pending'] > 0,
        ), $state->queues);
    }
```

```php
    /**
     * @return array<string, ThresholdData>
     */
    private function thresholdsOf(Environment $environment): array
    {
        $thresholds = [];

        foreach ($this->effectiveRules->forEnvironment($environment)->rules as $metric => $rule) {
            if ($rule->enabled) {
                $thresholds[$metric] = new ThresholdData($rule->threshold, $rule->severity);
            }
        }

        return $thresholds;
    }
```

```php
        public ?AlertSeverity $openAlertSeverity,
        public int $pendingTotal,
```

`app/Queries/WallQuery.php`, the whole file:

```php
<?php

namespace App\Queries;

use App\Data\Monitoring\AlertData;
use App\Data\Monitoring\EnvironmentData;
use App\Data\Pages\WallKpisData;
use App\Data\Pages\WallPageData;
use App\Enums\AlertRuleMetric;
use App\Enums\AlertSeverity;
use App\Enums\EnvironmentType;
use App\Enums\SeriesRange;
use App\Models\Team;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Monitoring\MonitoringRepository;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate;

class WallQuery
{
    public function __construct(private MonitoringRepository $monitoring) {}

    public function handle(Team $team, User $viewer): WallPageData
    {
        $environments = $this->monitoring->environments($team);
        usort($environments, EnvironmentData::compareBySeverityThenPending(...));

        $anomalies = $this->monitoring->openAlerts($team);
        $judged = array_values(array_filter($environments, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->isJudged()));
        $sum = fn (array $rows, callable $value) => array_sum(array_map($value, $rows));
        $failedRule = AlertRuleMetric::JobsFailedPerHour->value;
        $overFailedRate = array_values(array_filter(
            $judged,
            fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->failedLastHour > ($environment->thresholds[$failedRule]->value ?? INF),
        ));

        return new WallPageData(
            kpis: new WallKpisData(
                environmentsHealthy: count(array_filter($judged, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->isHealthy())),
                environmentsJudged: count($judged),
                environmentsNeedingAttention: count(array_filter($judged, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->needsAttention())),
                environmentsTotal: count($environments),
                openAnomalies: count($anomalies),
                openAlertSeverity: AlertSeverity::worstOf(array_map(fn (AlertData $alert) => $alert->severity, $anomalies)),
                pendingTotal: $sum($judged, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->pending),
                failedLastHour: $sum($judged, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->failedLastHour),
                failedLastHourCapped: array_any($judged, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->failedLastHourCapped),
                failedSeverity: AlertSeverity::worstOf(array_map(
                    fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->thresholds[$failedRule]->severity,
                    $overFailedRate,
                )),
                failedInWindow: $sum($judged, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->failedInWindow),
                failedWindowMinutes: $this->commonFailedWindow($judged === [] ? $environments : $judged),
            ),
            environments: $environments,
            anomalies: array_slice($anomalies, 0, config()->integer('horizon-watch.pages.wall_anomalies')),
            throughput: $this->monitoring->throughputSeries($team, null, SeriesRange::ThreeHours),
            grid: $this->monitoring->seriesGrid(SeriesRange::ThreeHours),
            jobsPerMinute: $sum($judged, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->jobsPerMinute),
            notifications: $this->monitoring->sentNotifications($team),
            applicationCount: count($this->monitoring->applications($team)),
            alertsReachNobody: $this->monitoring->notificationSummary($team)->reachesNobody,
            canManageAlertRules: Gate::forUser($viewer)->allows('manageAlertRules', $team),
            types: EnvironmentType::options(),
        );
    }

    /**
     * @param  array<int, EnvironmentData>  $environments
     */
    private function commonFailedWindow(array $environments): ?int
    {
        $read = array_filter($environments, fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->lastReadingAt !== null);
        $windows = array_unique(array_map(
            fn (EnvironmentData $environment) => $environment->failedWindowMinutes,
            $read === [] ? $environments : $read,
        ));

        return count($windows) === 1 ? reset($windows) : null;
    }
}
```

(`array_any` is available: `composer.json` requires PHP ^8.5. The `EnvironmentType` import and
the `types:` argument are Batch 1's (Task 1.5) and stay. Keep the `wall_anomalies` config
key; Batch 4 renames it. The window falls back to every environment when none is judged, so the
existing tests `an environment not read yet does not make the failed window mixed` and `with
nothing read yet the failed window is the default the rows carry` keep passing unchanged. The
snapshot factory defaults `failed_window_minutes` to 1440 and `failed_last_hour` to a random 0-5,
which is why every new test above sets `failed_last_hour` on every environment it records.)

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`resources/js/components/monitoring/environment/readings.ts`, the whole file. The precedence is
not visible > collection paused > reading error > stale > no reading yet > Horizon status. A
reading error reads "unreachable"; its reason is `readingErrorLabel`. "Stale" is read from the
server status, never from the raw `stale` flag (decision above): the server keeps a stale
environment last known down as `inactive`, and the chip, sort and counts must agree with it.
`stale` stays in `StateFields` only so the test above can prove the raw flag is ignored.

```ts
import { trans } from 'laravel-vue-i18n';
import { severityColor } from '@/lib/alerts';
import { formatCount, statusColor, statusLabel } from '@/lib/monitoring';

export type DisplayState =
    | 'hidden'
    | 'collection_off'
    | 'reading_error'
    | 'stale'
    | 'waiting'
    | App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus;

type StateFields = Pick<
    App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData,
    'status' | 'watched' | 'pollingEnabled' | 'readingError' | 'stale'
>;

const CALM: ReadonlyArray<DisplayState> = [
    'hidden',
    'collection_off',
    'waiting',
    'active',
];

export function displayState(environment: StateFields): DisplayState {
    if (!environment.watched) {
        return 'hidden';
    }

    if (!environment.pollingEnabled) {
        return 'collection_off';
    }

    if (environment.readingError !== null) {
        return 'reading_error';
    }

    if (environment.status === 'stale') {
        return 'stale';
    }

    return environment.status ?? 'waiting';
}

export function statusText(environment: StateFields): string {
    const state = displayState(environment);

    switch (state) {
        case 'hidden':
            return trans('Not on your wall');
        case 'collection_off':
            return trans('Collection paused');
        case 'reading_error':
            return statusLabel('unreachable');
        case 'waiting':
            return trans('No reading yet');
        default:
            return statusLabel(state);
    }
}

export function statusTone(environment: StateFields): string {
    const state = displayState(environment);

    switch (state) {
        case 'hidden':
        case 'collection_off':
        case 'waiting':
            return 'var(--nc-neutral-500)';
        case 'reading_error':
            return statusColor('unreachable');
        default:
            return statusColor(state);
    }
}

export function isHealthy(environment: StateFields): boolean {
    return displayState(environment) === 'active';
}

export function needsAttention(environment: StateFields): boolean {
    return !CALM.includes(displayState(environment));
}

export function readingErrorLabel(error: App.Enums.ReadingError): string {
    switch (error) {
        case 'unreachable':
            return trans('Horizon does not answer');
        case 'unauthorized':
            return trans('Horizon refused the credentials');
        case 'not_horizon':
            return trans('The address does not answer like Horizon');
        case 'blocked':
            return trans('This address is not allowed');
        case 'password_unreadable':
            return trans(
                'The stored password cannot be decrypted: enter it again',
            );
    }
}

export function hasMeasurement(
    environment: Pick<
        App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData,
        'status' | 'lastReadingAt' | 'readingError'
    >,
): boolean {
    return (
        environment.lastReadingAt !== null &&
        environment.readingError === null &&
        environment.status !== null &&
        environment.status !== 'unreachable'
    );
}

export function thresholdTone(
    environment: Pick<App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData, 'thresholds'>,
    metric: App.Enums.AlertRuleMetric,
    value: number,
): string | undefined {
    const threshold = environment.thresholds[metric] as
        | App.Data.Monitoring.ThresholdData
        | undefined;

    return threshold && value > threshold.value
        ? severityColor(threshold.severity)
        : undefined;
}

export function failedLastHourText(
    environment: Pick<
        App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData,
        'failedLastHour' | 'failedLastHourCapped'
    >,
): string {
    const count = formatCount(environment.failedLastHour);

    return environment.failedLastHourCapped
        ? trans('at least :count', { count })
        : count;
}

const SEVERITY: Record<App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus, number> = {
    inactive: 0,
    unreachable: 0,
    paused: 1,
    stale: 1,
    degraded: 2,
    active: 3,
};

export function worstTone(
    environments: Pick<App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData, 'status'>[],
): string | null {
    const statuses = environments
        .map((environment) => environment.status)
        .filter((status): status is App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus => !!status)
        .sort((a, b) => SEVERITY[a] - SEVERITY[b]);

    return statuses[0] ? statusColor(statuses[0]) : null;
}

export function troubledStyle(tone: string): Record<string, string> {
    return {
        background: `color-mix(in srgb, ${tone} 13%, var(--nc-surface))`,
        boxShadow: `0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, ${tone} 38%, transparent)`,
    };
}

export function calmStyle(): Record<string, string> {
    return {
        background: 'var(--nc-surface)',
        boxShadow: 'var(--nc-shadow-sm)',
        opacity: '0.82',
    };
}

export function formatAge(seconds: number): string {
    const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(seconds));

    if (value < 60) {
        return `${value} s`;
    }

    if (value < 3600) {
        return `${Math.floor(value / 60)} min`;
    }

    if (value < 172800) {
        return `${Math.floor(value / 3600)} h`;
    }

    return trans(':days d', { days: String(Math.floor(value / 86400)) });
}

export function secondsSince(iso: string, now: number): number {
    return Math.max(0, Math.floor((now - Date.parse(iso)) / 1000));
}

export function horizonStatusLabel(status: App.Enums.HorizonStatus): string {
    switch (status) {
        case 'running':
            return trans('running');
        case 'paused':
            return trans('paused');
        case 'inactive':
            return trans('inactive');
    }
}

const HORIZON_STATUS: Record<
    App.Enums.HorizonStatus,
    App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus
> = {
    running: 'active',
    paused: 'paused',
    inactive: 'inactive',
};

export function horizonStatusTone(
    environment: Pick<
        App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData,
        'horizonStatus' | 'readingError'
    >,
): string {
    if (environment.readingError !== null || environment.horizonStatus === null) {
        return 'var(--nc-neutral-500)';
    }

    return statusColor(HORIZON_STATUS[environment.horizonStatus]);
}
```

`resources/js/composables/useWallKpis.ts`:

```ts
import { trans } from 'laravel-vue-i18n';
import type { ComputedRef } from 'vue';
import { computed } from 'vue';
import { severityColor } from '@/lib/alerts';
import { failedWindowNote } from '@/lib/failedWindow';
import { formatCount } from '@/lib/monitoring';

export type WallKpiKey = 'healthy' | 'openAlerts' | 'pending' | 'failed';

export type WallKpi = {
    key: WallKpiKey;
    label: string;
    value: string;
    color?: string;
    note?: string;
};

export function useWallKpis(
    source: () => App.Data.Pages.WallKpisData,
): ComputedRef<WallKpi[]> {
    return computed(() => {
        const kpis = source();
        const failed = formatCount(kpis.failedLastHour);

        return [
            {
                key: 'healthy',
                label: trans('Healthy'),
                value: `${kpis.environmentsHealthy} / ${kpis.environmentsJudged}`,
                note: trans('across all applications'),
            },
            {
                key: 'openAlerts',
                label: trans('Open alerts'),
                value: String(kpis.openAnomalies),
                color: kpis.openAlertSeverity
                    ? severityColor(kpis.openAlertSeverity)
                    : undefined,
            },
            {
                key: 'pending',
                label: trans('Pending'),
                value: formatCount(kpis.pendingTotal),
                note: trans('sum of every queue'),
            },
            {
                key: 'failed',
                label: trans('Failed · last hour'),
                value: kpis.failedLastHourCapped
                    ? trans('at least :count', { count: failed })
                    : failed,
                color: kpis.failedSeverity
                    ? severityColor(kpis.failedSeverity)
                    : undefined,
                note: trans('Horizon: :count, :window', {
                    count: formatCount(kpis.failedInWindow),
                    window: failedWindowNote(kpis.failedWindowMinutes),
                }),
            },
        ];
    });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Create `resources/js/components/monitoring/environment/QueueFlags.vue`**

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { trans } from 'laravel-vue-i18n';
import { computed } from 'vue';
import { severityColor } from '@/lib/alerts';

const { queue, thresholds, quiet = false } = defineProps<{
    queue: Pick<
        App.Data.Monitoring.QueueData,
        'waitOverThreshold' | 'withoutWorkers'
    >;
    thresholds: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData['thresholds'];
    quiet?: boolean;
}>();

function flag(metric: App.Enums.AlertRuleMetric, label: string) {
    const threshold = thresholds[metric] as
        | App.Data.Monitoring.ThresholdData
        | undefined;
    const tone = threshold
        ? severityColor(threshold.severity)
        : 'var(--nc-neutral-400)';

    return {
        metric,
        label,
        style: {
            color: tone,
            background: `color-mix(in srgb, ${tone} 16%, transparent)`,
        },
    };
}

const flags = computed(() => [
    ...(queue.waitOverThreshold
        ? [flag('queue.max_wait', trans('wait over threshold'))]
        : []),
    ...(queue.withoutWorkers
        ? [flag('workers.missing', trans('no worker'))]
        : []),
]);
</script>

<template>
    <span v-if="flags.length" class="inline-flex flex-wrap gap-1">
        <span
            v-for="item in flags"
            :key="item.metric"
            class="nc-tag nc-tag-sm"
            :style="item.style"
            >{{ item.label }}</span
        >
    </span>
    <span v-else-if="!quiet" class="nc-tone-faint">—</span>
</template>
```
