```php
<?php

use Symfony\Component\Finder\Finder;

function stateAndNumbersSource(string $path): string
{
    return file_get_contents(resource_path('js/'.$path));
}

/**
 * @return array<string, string>
 */
function stateAndNumbersSources(): array
{
    $files = [];

    foreach (Finder::create()->files()->in(resource_path('js'))->name(['*.vue', '*.ts'])->notName('*.test.ts')->exclude(['generated', 'routes', 'actions', 'wayfinder', 'components/ui']) as $file) {
        $files[$file->getRelativePathname()] = $file->getContents();
    }

    return $files;
}

test('the last hour is the toned failed figure on the wall and the window count stays neutral', function (string $path) {
    expect(stateAndNumbersSource($path))
        ->toMatch("/thresholdTone\(\s*environment,\s*'jobs\.failed_per_hour',\s*environment\.failedLastHour,?\s*\)/")
        ->toContain('failedLastHourText(environment)')
        ->toContain('formatCount(environment.failedInWindow)')
        ->not->toMatch('/thresholdTone\([^)]*failedInWindow/')
        ->not->toContain('failedTone');
})->with([
    'wall tile' => 'components/monitoring/wall/EnvironmentTile.vue',
    'mobile wall row' => 'components/mobile/wall/MobileWall.vue',
]);

test('throughput carries its unit on the value on the wall and in the charts', function () {
    expect(stateAndNumbersSource('pages/monitoring/Wall.vue'))
        ->toContain("\$t(':value now', {")
        ->toContain('value: `${page.jobsPerMinute}/min`')
        ->toContain("trans(':range, peak :value', {")
        ->toContain('const describeThroughput = (value: number) => `${value}/min`;')
        ->not->toContain('jobs/min');

    expect(stateAndNumbersSource('components/monitoring/environment/TrendChart.vue'))
        ->toContain("<figcaption class=\"caption\">{{ \$t('Throughput') }}</figcaption>")
        ->toContain("trans(':range, peak :value', {")
        ->toContain('const describe = (value: number) => `${value}/min`;')
        ->not->toContain('jobs/min');

    expect(stateAndNumbersSource('components/mobile/wall/MobileWall.vue'))
        ->not->toMatch('#jobs/min#i');
});
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/vue3';
import { PhMinus, PhTrendDown, PhTrendUp } from '@phosphor-icons/vue';
import { computed } from 'vue';
import EnvPill from '@/components/nocturne/EnvPill.vue';
import TrendLine from '@/components/nocturne/TrendLine.vue';
import MaintenanceBadge from '@/components/monitoring/MaintenanceBadge.vue';
import {
    calmStyle,
    displayState,
    failedLastHourText,
    hasMeasurement,
    needsAttention,
    statusText,
    statusTone,
    thresholdTone,
    troubledStyle,
} from '@/components/monitoring/environment/readings';
import { useEnvironmentHref } from '@/composables/useEnvironmentHref';
import { failedWindowNote, failedWindowShort } from '@/lib/failedWindow';
import { formatCount, formatWait, statusIcon } from '@/lib/monitoring';

const { environment } = defineProps<{
    environment: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData;
}>();

const environmentHref = useEnvironmentHref();

const troubled = computed(() => needsAttention(environment));
const tint = computed(() => statusTone(environment));
const showsState = computed(() => displayState(environment) !== 'active');
const measured = computed(() => hasMeasurement(environment));

const tileStyle = computed(() =>
    troubled.value ? troubledStyle(tint.value) : calmStyle(),
);

const urgent = computed(
    () =>
        environment.status === 'inactive' ||
        environment.status === 'unreachable',
);

const trend = computed(() => {
    const percent = environment.trendPercent;

    if (percent === null || percent === 0) {
        return { icon: PhMinus, label: percent === 0 ? '0%' : '' };
    }

    return percent > 0
        ? { icon: PhTrendUp, label: `+${percent}%` }
        : { icon: PhTrendDown, label: `${percent}%` };
});
</script>

            >
            <span class="nc-micro nc-tone-faint">{{ $t('pending') }}</span>
            <span
                class="nc-t-xs ml-auto"
                :style="{
                    color:
                        thresholdTone(
                            environment,
                            'queue.max_wait',
                            environment.maxWaitSeconds,

                }"
                >{{
```

```ts
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/vue3';
import { PhCaretDown, PhCaretRight } from '@phosphor-icons/vue';
import { computed } from 'vue';
import AttentionBadge from '@/components/monitoring/AttentionBadge.vue';
import EnvironmentTile from '@/components/monitoring/wall/EnvironmentTile.vue';
import {
    needsAttention,
    statusText,
    statusTone,
} from '@/components/monitoring/environment/readings';
import { useTeamSlug } from '@/composables/useTeamSlug';
import { envTypeColor, formatCount } from '@/lib/monitoring';
import { show as showApplication } from '@/routes/applications';

const { applicationId, applicationName, environments } = defineProps<{
    applicationId: string;
    applicationName: string;
    environments: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData[];
}>();

const forced = defineModel<boolean | undefined>('expanded');

const slug = useTeamSlug();

const troubled = computed(() => environments.filter(needsAttention));

const expanded = computed(() => forced.value ?? troubled.value.length > 0);

const pending = computed(() =>
    environments.reduce((total, environment) => total + environment.pending, 0),
);

function dotLabel(environment: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData): string {
    return `${environment.name} · ${statusText(environment)}`;
}

function dotStyle(environment: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData) {
    const halo = needsAttention(environment)
        ? `0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, ${statusTone(environment)} 55%, transparent)`
        : undefined;

    return { background: envTypeColor(environment.type), boxShadow: halo };
}
```

```vue
import { formatCount, formatWait, statusIcon } from '@/lib/monitoring';

    rows,
    totalCount,
    attentionCount,
    waitingCount,
    typeLabel,
    search,
    kpis,
} = defineProps<{
    rows: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData[];
    totalCount: number;
    attentionCount: number;
    waitingCount: number;
    typeLabel: string;
    search: string;
    kpis: App.Data.Pages.WallKpisData;
}>();

const emit = defineEmits<{ clear: [] }>();

const filter = defineModel<'all' | 'problems'>('filter', { required: true });

const slug = useTeamSlug();

const wallKpis = useWallKpis(() => kpis);
const tiles = computed(() =>
    wallKpis.value.filter((kpi) => MOBILE_KPIS.includes(kpi.key)),
);

const narrowing = computed(() =>
    [typeLabel, search.trim() ? `"${search.trim()}"` : '']
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(' · '),
);

function rowStyle(environment: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData) {

}
```

```php
test('the queue table shows contributor flags instead of a status that re-applies the rules', function () {
    expect(stateAndNumbersSource('components/monitoring/environment/QueueTable.vue'))
        ->toContain("<th>{{ \$t('Flags') }}</th>")
        ->toContain('<QueueFlags')
        ->not->toContain("\$t('Status')")
        ->not->toContain('queue.status')
        ->not->toContain('waitThreshold');

    expect(property_exists(QueueData::class, 'status'))->toBeFalse();
});

test('a long-running job takes the runtime rule severity, with no 300 s step', function () {
    expect(stateAndNumbersSource('components/monitoring/environment/LongRunningJobs.vue'))
        ->toMatch("/thresholdTone\(\s*\{\s*thresholds\s*\},\s*'job\.runtime',\s*seconds\s*\)/")
        ->not->toContain('seconds > 300')
        ->not->toMatch('/var\(--st-(?:ok|warn|down)\)/');
});

test('an inactive Horizon is the banner headline, with the missing master supervisor as its explanation', function () {
    $banner = stateAndNumbersSource('components/monitoring/environment/IncidentBanner.vue');
    $headline = strpos($banner, "\$t('Horizon inactive')");
    $explanation = strpos($banner, "'No active master supervisor: jobs stay pending until one starts again.'");

    expect($headline)->toBeInt()
        ->and($explanation)->toBeInt()
        ->and($headline)->toBeLessThan($explanation)
        ->and($banner)->not->toContain("\$t('No active master supervisor')")
        ->not->toContain('No active workers');
});

test('a reading error has one label helper and no template chain', function () {
    expect(method_exists(ReadingError::class, 'label'))->toBeFalse();

    $labels = [
        'Horizon does not answer',
        'Horizon refused the credentials',
        'The address does not answer like Horizon',
        'This address is not allowed',
        'The stored password cannot be decrypted: enter it again',
    ];
    $helper = 'components/monitoring/environment/readings.ts';

    $chains = array_keys(array_filter(
        stateAndNumbersSources(),
        fn (string $source, string $path) => $path !== $helper && (
            preg_match("/(?:readingError|\.error)\s*===\s*'(?:unreachable|not_horizon|blocked|password_unreadable)'/", $source) === 1
            || array_any($labels, fn (string $label) => str_contains($source, "'{$label}'"))
        ),
        ARRAY_FILTER_USE_BOTH,
    ));
    sort($chains);

    expect($chains)->toBe([]);

    foreach ($labels as $label) {
        expect(stateAndNumbersSource($helper))->toContain("'{$label}'");
    }
});

test('no surface writes throughput as jobs/min', function () {
    $worded = array_keys(array_filter(
        stateAndNumbersSources(),
        fn (string $source) => preg_match('#jobs/min#i', $source) === 1,
    ));
    sort($worded);

    expect($worded)->toBe([]);
});
```

(`'unauthorized'` is left out of the comparison pattern on purpose: `ConnectionCheckRow.vue`
checks `result.error === 'unauthorized'` once to offer the credentials fields, which is not a
label chain. The label check catches a chain that starts with it anyway. The labels are matched
as quoted strings, not as `trans('…')` calls, because the formatter breaks the password label's
`trans(` call over two lines in `readings.ts`.)

```ts
type Tile = { label: string; value: string; color?: string; note?: string };

const tiles = computed<Tile[]>(() => [
    {
        label: trans('Master'),
        value:
            environment.value.horizonStatus !== null
                ? horizonStatusLabel(environment.value.horizonStatus)
                : environment.value.status === null
                  ? statusText(environment.value)
                  : trans('unknown'),
        color: horizonStatusTone(environment.value),
        note:
            environment.value.readingError !== null &&
            environment.value.horizonStatus !== null
                ? trans('last known')
                : trans('nodes: :count', {
                      count: String(environment.value.nodeCount),
                  }),
    },
    {
        label: trans('Pending'),
        value: formatCount(environment.value.pending),
        color: thresholdTone(
            environment.value,
            'queue.pending',
            environment.value.pending,
        ),
        note: transChoice(':count queue|:count queues', page.queues.length),
    },
    {
        label: trans('Max wait'),
        value: formatWait(environment.value.maxWaitSeconds),
        color: thresholdTone(
            environment.value,
            'queue.max_wait',
            environment.value.maxWaitSeconds,
        ),
        note: maxWaitNote.value,
    },
    {
        label: trans('Workers'),
        value: String(environment.value.workers),
        note: trans('active processes'),
    },
    {
        label: trans('Throughput'),
        value: `${environment.value.jobsPerMinute}/min`,
    },
    {
        label: trans('Failed · last hour'),
        value: failedLastHourText(environment.value),
        color: thresholdTone(
            environment.value,
            'jobs.failed_per_hour',
            environment.value.failedLastHour,
        ),
        note: trans('Horizon: :count, :window', {
            count: formatCount(environment.value.failedInWindow),
            window: failedWindowNote(environment.value.failedWindowMinutes),
        }),
    },
]);
```

## Batch 3: One formatter per kind and the webhook summary wording

Goal: every duration, relative time, threshold, alert value and instant in the product goes
through one formatter of its kind. Durations become floor based, spaced and limited to two
translatable units (`45 s`, `1 min 30 s`, `1 h 5 min`, `2 d 3 h`, a day from 24 h) in
TypeScript (`formatSeconds`) and PHP (`App\Support\Duration`, mirrored by `AlertMail`, and
therefore by the webhook `summary`). The compact form survives only on chart axes. "… ago" is
built on the same helper (`formatAgo`). Thresholds and alert values are exact, locale-grouped
numbers (`formatNumber` / `Number::format`, two decimals at most) and keep their input unit
(`> 60 s`). Instants go through one `formatInstant` that adds weekday, day and month when not
today. The README webhook example and the CHANGELOG record the new `summary` wording.

Spec themes covered: **6** (durations, numbers and times), plus the webhook `summary` wording
constraint and the theme 19 README example for it.

Batches 1 and 2 have already run: `envTypeColor`, `lib/environments.ts`, the `readings.ts`
display-state helpers, `useWallKpis.ts` and the threshold severities exist. Where this batch
edits a file that an earlier batch also touched, the steps name only the import names and
expressions to swap, so they apply whatever else is around them. Line numbers in this part are
those of the file on `release/1.0` before Batch 1: where Batch 1, Batch 2 or an earlier task of
this batch edits the same file (`lib/monitoring.ts`, `lib/alertRules.ts`, `readings.ts`,
`readings.test.ts`, `NotificationSettings.vue`, `CHANGELOG.md`, …), locate the block by the
function name or the code quoted with it. Batches 4 to 8 have not run:
`AnomalyList.vue`, `EnvironmentComparison.vue`, `IncidentBanner.vue`'s "started" line,
`formatRelative` and the "Silence for…" copy still exist and are handled here only where they
format a duration or a time.

Decisions taken where the spec leaves a detail open (one line each, repeated in the task that
applies them):

- `formatAgo(seconds)` keeps one unit, and says "less than a minute ago" under 60 s, so minute
  sources (`minutesAgo * 60`) read exactly as `formatElapsed` did.
- Sentences that already carry "… ago" around a `:time` (freshness, node seen, scheduler) keep
  their keys and get `formatSeconds(seconds, 1)`, so they keep their per-second precision.
- Thresholds and alert values use two decimals at most in TypeScript too (`formatNumber`),
  matching `AlertMail::number` (`maxPrecision: 2`).
- The failed-jobs window fragment is `formatSeconds(windowMinutes * 60)` in
  `failedWindowShort` (`1 d`, `7 d`, `1 h`); Batch 2 already deleted `failedLabel`. Days start
  from 24 h, as the rule says.
- The alert repeat interval is a duration too: `every 30 min while open`, `every 1 h while open`.
- The average runtime column of the queue table keeps one decimal under a minute (`0.4 s`):
  Horizon reports sub-second runtimes, and flooring them would show `0 s`.
- Pending invitations: "Sent" uses `formatAgo`, "Expires" uses `formatInstant`; the
  `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` helper `formatRelative` is deleted.
- The resolution email's "open for" is computed from whole seconds (`diffInSeconds`), floored.
- `formatSecondsCompact` is `formatSeconds(seconds, 1)` without the space (`30s`, `2min`,
  `12h`, `2d`); every axis tick of `niceSecondsMax` is a whole single unit.
- Italian "queue :queue · started at :time" becomes "queue :queue · avvio :time", because the
  instant can now carry a weekday (`avvio ven 16 ott, 06:00`).
- The trend chart's range switch is a duration on screen, so its labels go through
  `formatSeconds`: `3 h`, `1 d`, `7 d` (were `3h`, `24h`, `7 d`); the range values sent to the
  server (`3h`, `24h`, `7d`) do not change.
- Two clocks stay outside `formatInstant`: the header's "updated :time" stamp
  (`useLastRefresh`, always today, keeps its seconds because the panel refreshes every 5 to
  300 s) and the chart hover labels (`formatBucketTime`, part of the chart like its axes).

New shared names introduced by this batch (not in the registry):

- `formatNumber(value: number): string` in `resources/js/lib/monitoring.ts`.
- `formatRuleFor(minutes: number): string` in `resources/js/lib/alertRules.ts` (named by the
  spec, replaces `alertRules.formatDuration`).
- `quietHoursSummary(from: string | null, to: string | null, timezone: string): string` in
  `resources/js/lib/datetime.ts` (named by the spec).
- `formatInstant(iso, locale, now?: Date)`: the registry signature plus an optional `now`, used
  only by tests.

Commit: one commit at the end of the batch (Task 3.11). Tasks 3.1 to 3.10 are not committed
separately.

### Task 3.1: lang/it.json key helper (container scratch file, not committed)

Every later task that renames an English source string renames its `lang/it.json` key in the
same task, through this helper. It keeps the file sorted the way it is today (`ksort`,
`SORT_STRING`) and pretty-printed byte for byte as now (checked: a load and save without
changes leaves the file identical).

**Files:**

- Create (inside the container only, not in the repo): `/tmp/it-keys.php`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: `php /tmp/it-keys.php lang/it.json '<json>'`, where `<json>` is
  `{"remove": [<keys>], "add": {<key>: <italian>}}`. Removing runs before adding, so a key
  whose Italian value changes is listed in both. It exits 1 on a key to remove that does not
  exist, or a key to add that exists with another value.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the helper into the container**

```bash
docker compose exec -T -u sail laravel.test bash -lc 'cat > /tmp/it-keys.php' <<'PHP'
<?php
[, $path, $changes] = $argv;
$keys = json_decode(file_get_contents($path), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
$changes = json_decode($changes, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
foreach ($changes['remove'] as $key) {
    if (! array_key_exists($key, $keys)) {
        fwrite(STDERR, "missing key: {$key}\n");
        exit(1);
    }
    unset($keys[$key]);
}
foreach ($changes['add'] as $key => $italian) {
    if (array_key_exists($key, $keys) && $keys[$key] !== $italian) {
        fwrite(STDERR, "key already present: {$key}\n");
        exit(1);
    }
    $keys[$key] = $italian;
}
ksort($keys, SORT_STRING);
file_put_contents($path, json_encode($keys, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES)."\n");
echo 'lang/it.json: '.count($changes['remove']).' removed, '.count($changes['add'])." added\n";
PHP
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Check it is a no-op on an empty change**

- [ ] **Step 2: Run it and see it fail**

Run: `docker compose exec -T -u sail laravel.test bash -lc 'php artisan test --compact --filter="DurationTest"'`

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `app/Support/Duration.php`:

```php
<?php

namespace App\Support;

final class Duration
{
    /**
     * Seconds in a day, an hour, a minute and a second, largest first.
     */
    private const array SIZES = [86400, 3600, 60, 1];

    /**
     * A duration rounded down to at most $parts units, each spaced from its number:
     * 45 s, 1 min 30 s, 1 h 5 min, 2 d 3 h. The TypeScript formatSeconds() mirrors it.
     */
    public static function format(int $seconds, int $parts = 2): string
    {
        $total = max(0, $seconds);
        $index = 0;

        while ($index < count(self::SIZES) - 1 && $total < self::SIZES[$index]) {
            $index++;
        }

        $size = self::SIZES[$index];
        $text = self::unit($size, intdiv($total, $size));
        $next = self::SIZES[$index + 1] ?? null;

        if ($parts < 2 || $next === null) {
            return $text;
        }

        $minor = intdiv($total % $size, $next);

        return $minor > 0 ? $text.' '.self::unit($next, $minor) : $text;
    }

    private static function unit(int $size, int $count): string
    {
        $value = (string) $count;

        return match ($size) {
            86400 => __(':days d', ['days' => $value]),
            3600 => __(':hours h', ['hours' => $value]),
            60 => __(':minutes min', ['minutes' => $value]),
            default => __(':seconds s', ['seconds' => $value]),
        };
    }
}
```

The keys are literal `__()` calls on purpose: `TranslationsTest` finds them, and PHPStan types
them as strings as it does in `AlertMail`.

Expected: PASS, 14 tests (12 dataset rows and the two other tests).

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `resources/js/lib/monitoring.ts`, add after `formatCount`:

```ts
const DURATION_UNITS: readonly {
    size: number;
    label: (value: string) => string;
}[] = [
    { size: 86400, label: (days) => trans(':days d', { days }) },
    { size: 3600, label: (hours) => trans(':hours h', { hours }) },
    { size: 60, label: (minutes) => trans(':minutes min', { minutes }) },
    { size: 1, label: (seconds) => trans(':seconds s', { seconds }) },
];

/**
 * A duration rounded down to at most two units, each spaced from its number:
 * 45 s, 1 min 30 s, 1 h 5 min, 2 d 3 h. App\Support\Duration mirrors it.
 */
export function formatSeconds(seconds: number, parts: 1 | 2 = 2): string {
    const total = Number.isFinite(seconds)
        ? Math.max(0, Math.floor(seconds))
        : 0;
    const index = DURATION_UNITS.findIndex(({ size }) => total >= size);
    const major =
        DURATION_UNITS[index === -1 ? DURATION_UNITS.length - 1 : index];
    const minor =
        parts === 2 && index !== -1 ? DURATION_UNITS[index + 1] : undefined;
    const text = major.label(String(Math.floor(total / major.size)));

    if (minor === undefined) {
        return text;
    }

    const count = Math.floor((total % major.size) / minor.size);

    return count > 0 ? `${text} ${minor.label(String(count))}` : text;
}

/** Chart axes only: one unit, no space (30s, 2min, 12h, 2d). */
export function formatSecondsCompact(seconds: number): string {
    return formatSeconds(seconds, 1).replace(' ', '');
}

export function formatAgo(seconds: number): string {
    return seconds < 60
        ? trans('less than a minute ago')
        : trans(':time ago', { time: formatSeconds(seconds, 1) });
}

/** Thresholds and alert values: exact and grouped, like AlertMail::number(). */
export function formatNumber(value: number): string {
    return new Intl.NumberFormat(getActiveLanguage(), {
        maximumFractionDigits: 2,
    }).format(value);
}
```

Create `resources/js/lib/datetime.ts`:

```ts
import { trans } from 'laravel-vue-i18n';

/** An instant in the viewer's zone: the time today, weekday, day and month otherwise. */
export function formatInstant(
    iso: string,
    locale: string,
    now: Date = new Date(),
): string {
    const at = new Date(iso);
    const today = at.toDateString() === now.toDateString();

    return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
        ...(today ? {} : { weekday: 'short', day: 'numeric', month: 'short' }),
        hour: '2-digit',
        minute: '2-digit',
        hourCycle: 'h23',
    }).format(at);
}

export function quietHoursSummary(
```

```ts
export function formatThreshold(threshold: number, unit: string): string {
```

## Batch 4: One vocabulary: alerts, maintenance, notifications, people, accounts

Goal: every concept the panel shows has one name, in English and in Italian, and the code calls it
by that name too. The object is an **alert**, which is **opened** and **resolved**; the action is
**Mark as handled**. The leftover "anomaly" identifiers become alert ones (`alert:handle`,
`handleAlert`, `OpenAlertList`, `openAlerts`, config `wall_alerts` with a fallback). Every alert
list takes its icon and tone from one `alertTone` / `alertIcon` pair, and the comparator and the
state-rule flag come from the server. "Mute" is only the per-alert action; whatever creates a
maintenance window says "maintenance"; quiet hours are "Fascia di quiete". The delivery tests live
only in Alert settings, non-managers read the delivery policy, the admin list is "Extra
addresses", the webhook key is always the "signing secret", delivery errors are sentences, and
an opening email prints its value once. Role and visibility labels come from the server, with
Italian role names, and leaving an organization is one action. One password policy description
is built next to `Password::defaults()`, and the account screens say "Log in" / "Log out",
"Name" / "Email".

Spec themes covered: **7** (alert vocabulary), **8** (suppression vocabulary), **13**
(notifications and delivery), **14** (people, roles, visibility), **16** (account and
authentication), with their `lang/it.json` keys.

Batches 1 to 3 have run when this batch starts: `EnvironmentType`, `readings.ts` with
`statusText` / `DisplayState`, `useWallKpis.ts`, `formatSeconds`, `formatAgo`, `formatInstant`,
`formatRuleFor`, `quietHoursSummary` and `lib/datetime.ts` exist; the alert lists format their
ages with `formatAgo(… * 60)`. Batches 5 to 8 have not run: `IncidentBanner.vue` still has its
"started" and "Rule:" lines, `SilenceMenu.vue` keeps its name, README, CHANGELOG and the
CONTRIBUTING glossary still describe the old wording. Where this batch edits a file an earlier
batch also touched, each step quotes only the lines it replaces, so it applies whatever else is
around them.

All commands run from the repo root `/home/mmarretti@enegan.locale/MyProjects/horizon-watch`.
PHP, Node and the test runners run in the Sail container (`docker compose up -d` first); `git`,
`grep` and `sed` run on the host. Line numbers are those of commit `34f47ac`; every edit is
anchored on quoted text as well.

Decisions taken where the spec leaves a detail open (each repeated in the task that applies it):

- The wall's list prop is `WallPageData::$alerts` (was `$anomalies`); the KPI is
  `WallKpisData::$openAlerts` (was `$openAnomalies`), as the spec names it. `OpenAlertList`
  takes `alerts`.
- "Open alerts" is "Alert aperti" in Italian (wall list, KPI, alerts tab); the two other tabs
  follow: "Alert silenziati", "Alert risolti".
- The `wall_anomalies` fallback is read in `WallQuery`: `wall_alerts` wins, else
  `wall_anomalies`, else 5. The config file ships only `wall_alerts`.
- `alertTone`: resolved → `var(--st-ok)`, muted → `var(--nc-neutral-500)`, open → the severity
  colour. An open "Horizon paused" alert is a warning and so amber; the wall list's special
  `--st-off` case goes. `alertIcon`: resolved → `PhCheckCircle`, otherwise the rule icon.
- In the alert log table the Severity cell keeps the severity word and takes the icon and
  tone from `alertIcon` / `alertTone`; `severityIcon` has no caller left and is deleted.
- `AlertData::$environmentStatus` stays in the payload (only the client colouring goes):
  trimming it is not in theme 17's list and other tests pin it.
- `formatRule` takes the rule object (`metric`, `threshold`, `unit`, `comparator`), so the
  comparator always comes from the server.
- The application page's empty "Recent alerts" box says "No open or recent alerts on the
  environments you can see.", because it lists open, muted and recently resolved alerts.
- "until it clears" becomes "until it is resolved" in the three delivery sentences (the alert
  is resolved, per the theme 7 rule).
- Theme 8 renames copy only: the route `environments.silence`, `SilenceMenu.vue` and
  `silenceChoices` keep their names.

### Task 4.1: lang/it.json key helper (container scratch file, not committed)

Every task below that renames, adds or removes an English source string changes its
`lang/it.json` key in the same task through this helper. It is the same helper as Batch 3's
Task 3.1, written again because `/tmp` does not survive a container restart. It keeps the file
sorted as today (`ksort`, `SORT_STRING`) and byte-identical on a no-op (checked on `34f47ac`).

**Files:**

- Create (inside the container only, not in the repo): `/tmp/it-keys.php`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: `php /tmp/it-keys.php lang/it.json '<json>'`, with `<json>` =
  `{"remove": [<keys>], "add": {<key>: <italian>}}`. Removing runs before adding, so a key whose
  Italian changes is listed in both. Exit 1 on a key to remove that does not exist, or on a key to
  add that exists with another value. Every task calls it the same way, feeding the JSON on
  stdin:

```bash
docker compose exec -T -u sail laravel.test bash -lc 'php /tmp/it-keys.php lang/it.json "$(cat)"' <<'JSON'
{"remove": [], "add": {}}
JSON
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the helper into the container**

```bash
docker compose exec -T -u sail laravel.test bash -lc 'cat > /tmp/it-keys.php' <<'PHP'
<?php
[, $path, $changes] = $argv;
$keys = json_decode(file_get_contents($path), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
$changes = json_decode($changes, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
foreach ($changes['remove'] as $key) {
    if (! array_key_exists($key, $keys)) {
        fwrite(STDERR, "missing key: {$key}\n");
        exit(1);
    }
    unset($keys[$key]);
}
foreach ($changes['add'] as $key => $italian) {
    if (array_key_exists($key, $keys) && $keys[$key] !== $italian) {
        fwrite(STDERR, "key already present: {$key}\n");
        exit(1);
    }
    $keys[$key] = $italian;
}
ksort($keys, SORT_STRING);
file_put_contents($path, json_encode($keys, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES)."\n");
echo 'lang/it.json: '.count($changes['remove']).' removed, '.count($changes['add'])." added\n";
PHP
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Check it is a no-op on an empty change**

```bash
docker compose exec -T -u sail laravel.test bash -lc 'php /tmp/it-keys.php lang/it.json "$(cat)"' <<'JSON'
{"remove": [], "add": {}}
JSON
git diff --stat lang/it.json
```

Expected: `lang/it.json: 0 removed, 0 added` and no diff. If the container restarts later in the
batch, repeat Step 1.

```php
}
```

alert list: the wall's `OpenAlertList`, `EnvironmentAlerts`, `RecentAlerts`, `AlertTable`,
`AlertCards`. The environment status never colours an alert row. `AlertMarks` always renders in
`RecentAlerts`. The button says "Mark as handled". The banner says "opened". The first-run card

```ts
export function alertTone(alert: App.Data.Monitoring.AlertData): string {
    switch (alert.state) {
        case 'resolved':
            return 'var(--st-ok)';
        case 'muted':
            return 'var(--nc-neutral-500)';
        case 'open':
            return severityColor(alert.severity);
    }
}

export function alertIcon(alert: App.Data.Monitoring.AlertData): Component {
    return alert.state === 'resolved' ? PhCheckCircle : ruleIcon(alert.metric);
}
```

### Task 4.8: Notifications: tests only in Alert settings, one delivery policy, "Extra addresses"

The email and webhook tests live only in Alert settings: `DeliveryTest` is deleted from the
Alerts page and its footnote moves under the test buttons. Non-managers see the read-only
`DeliveryPolicy` on Alert settings instead of the second grid of `NotificationSettings`. The
"Email is not set up" notice is shown by `DeliveryPolicy`, and its target lines hide while
`AudienceWarning` says nobody is reached. The admin list is "Extra addresses" (label, validation
attribute, permission row), and the webhook key is the "signing secret" in the two strings that
still said "webhook secret" / "new secret".

Decisions: `NotificationSettings` renders only for managers and takes a non-null `settings`; it
keeps its own "Email is not set up" notice, since it never shares a page with `DeliveryPolicy`.
The permission row "Edit thresholds and recipients" becomes "Edit thresholds and notifications".
The read-only grid's `:count member|:count members` loses its last caller and is removed. The
maintenance-window validation attribute `target` keeps its English key but its Italian
"destinazione" becomes "ambito", so that "destinazione" names only a place a notification goes.

### Task 4.9: Delivery errors are sentences, never enum codes

The delivery log on the wall printed `trans('http_4xx')`, `trans('timeout')`, `trans('mail')`:
enum codes used as translation keys, one of them (`unreachable`) shared with the environment
status. Every `DeliveryError` gets a sentence key, in one helper `deliveryErrorLabel` in
`lib/alerts.ts`; `SentNotifications.vue` uses it. The `unreachable` key stays, now only for the
environment status label.

Decision: an answered HTTP status still wins (`HTTP 404`), as today.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the helper**

In `resources/js/lib/alerts.ts`, after `channelLabel`:

```ts
export function deliveryErrorLabel(
    error: App.Enums.DeliveryError,
    httpStatus: number | null,
): string {
    if (httpStatus !== null) {
        return `HTTP ${httpStatus}`;
    }

    switch (error) {
        case 'timeout':
            return trans('the destination did not answer in time');
        case 'blocked':
            return trans(
                'the address points to a network the panel does not call',
            );
        case 'http_3xx':
            return trans('redirect not followed');
        case 'http_4xx':
            return trans('refused by the destination');
        case 'http_5xx':
            return trans('error at the destination');
        case 'unreachable':
            return trans('destination unreachable');
        case 'mail':
            return trans('the email could not be sent');
        case 'mail_unreachable':
            return trans('mail server unreachable');
        case 'mail_authentication':
            return trans('mail server refused the login');
        case 'mail_rejected':
            return trans('refused by the mail server');
        case 'secret_unreadable':
            return trans('signing secret unreadable, regenerate it');
        case 'no_longer_due':
            return trans('alert resolved, handled or muted first');
        case 'opening_not_delivered':
            return trans('its opening never reached this destination');
    }
}
```

`resources/js/components/monitoring/wall/SentNotifications.vue`:

- `import { channelIcon } from '@/lib/alerts';` →
  `import { channelIcon, deliveryErrorLabel } from '@/lib/alerts';`

- in `outcome()`, `` `${status} · ${errorLabel(notification.error, notification.httpStatus)}` ``

### Task 4.10: Role and visibility labels come from the server, in Italian too

The client copies in `lib/members.ts` (`ASSIGNABLE_ROLES`, `VISIBILITIES`, `visibilityLabel`,
`assignableRoleName`) go. `MembersPageData` sends `roles`, `assignableRoles` and `visibilities`
as `{value, label}` options built from `TeamRole::label()` and `MemberVisibility::label()`. The
invite form's radios (which printed the raw `admin` / `member` / `viewer`), the member menu and
the permission matrix's column headers (which printed the raw keys) use them. The four roles are
translated: Proprietario, Amministratore, Membro, Osservatore, and the Italian prose follows.

Decision: the owner's label is "Owner" (was "Owner · admin"), since "Admin" names only the
organization role. `TeamRole::assignable()` returns admin, member, viewer, the same set the
`Rule::enum(...)->except(TeamRole::Owner)` validation accepts.

- [ ] **Step 3: Compute the flag on the server**

`app/Data/Teams/UserTeamData.php`, after `public bool $isCurrent,`:

```php
        public bool $isLastAdmin,
```

`app/Concerns/HasTeams.php`: replace `toUserTeams()` and `toUserTeam()` with:

```php
    /**
     * @return Collection<int, UserTeamData>
     */
    public function toUserTeams(bool $includeCurrent = false): Collection
    {
        $teams = $this->teams()->get();
        $admins = $this->adminCounts($teams
            ->filter(fn (Team $team) => $this->teamRole($team) === TeamRole::Admin)
            ->map(fn (Team $team): int => $team->id)
            ->values()
            ->all());

        return $teams
            ->map(fn (Team $team) => ! $includeCurrent && $this->isCurrentTeam($team) ? null : $this->toUserTeam($team, $admins[$team->id] ?? 0))
            ->filter()
            ->values();
    }

    public function toUserTeam(Team $team, ?int $adminCount = null): UserTeamData
    {
        $role = $this->teamRole($team);

        if ($role === TeamRole::Admin) {
            $adminCount ??= $this->adminCounts([$team->id])[$team->id] ?? 0;
        }

        return new UserTeamData(
            id: $team->id,
            name: $team->name,
            slug: $team->slug,
            role: $role,
            roleLabel: $role?->label(),
            isCurrent: $this->isCurrentTeam($team),
            isLastAdmin: $role === TeamRole::Admin && $adminCount === 1,
        );
    }

    /**
     * @param  array<int, int>  $teamIds
     * @return array<int, int>
     */
    private function adminCounts(array $teamIds): array
    {
        if ($teamIds === []) {
            return [];
        }

        return Membership::query()
            ->whereIn('team_id', $teamIds)
            ->where('role', TeamRole::Admin->value)
            ->groupBy('team_id')
            ->selectRaw('team_id, count(*) as admins')
            ->pluck('admins', 'team_id')
            ->map(fn (mixed $count): int => (int) $count)
            ->all();
    }
```

### Task 4.13: One password policy description, shown wherever a password is chosen

`App\Support\PasswordPolicy` holds the minimum length, the rule (`Password::min(10)->letters()
->numbers()`, which `Password::defaults()` now returns) and the sentence "At least :min
characters, with letters and numbers". `PasswordPolicyData {rules, description}` carries the
`passwordrules` string and the sentence to Setup, Invitation, Reset password (the Fortify view
gets the prop) and Security, where the sentence is helper text under the new password.

Decisions: the sentence replaces the "at least 10 characters" placeholders; the reset page's
`passwordRules` prop, declared but never sent, is replaced by `passwordPolicy`; Security's
`passwordRules` prop is replaced by `passwordPolicy` too.

- [ ] **Step 3: The policy, next to `Password::defaults()`**

Create `app/Support/PasswordPolicy.php`:

```php
<?php

namespace App\Support;

use Illuminate\Validation\Rules\Password;

final class PasswordPolicy
{
    public const int MIN_LENGTH = 10;

    public static function rule(): Password
    {
        return Password::min(self::MIN_LENGTH)->letters()->numbers();
    }

    public static function description(): string
    {
        return __('At least :min characters, with letters and numbers', ['min' => self::MIN_LENGTH]);
    }
}
```

Create `app/Data/Auth/PasswordPolicyData.php`:

```php
<?php

namespace App\Data\Auth;

use App\Support\PasswordPolicy;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rules\Password;
use Spatie\LaravelData\Data;

class PasswordPolicyData extends Data
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $rules,
        public string $description,
    ) {}

    public static function current(): self
    {
        return new self(
            rules: Password::default()->toPasswordRulesString(),
            description: PasswordPolicy::description(),
        );
    }
}
```

## Batch 5: Pages say each thing once; one environment form; real forms and actions

Goal: every monitoring page states each fact once, every environment form behaves the same in the
wizard, on Add environment and on Edit environment, and every form in the panel submits on Enter,
lays out one right-aligned action row, gates Save on changes, marks destructive triggers with the
danger tone, and reports errors through `InputError` (field) or `FormErrors` (form level). Spec
themes covered: 9 (environment page), 10 (application page and entry points), 11 (one environment
form), 12 (forms, actions, destructive operations, errors).

All commands run from the repo root `/home/mmarretti@enegan.locale/MyProjects/horizon-watch`,
inside the Sail containers. Tasks 5.1 to 5.13 are committed together in Task 5.14 (one commit for
the batch).

### Assumptions about Batches 1 to 4

Batches 1 to 4 run before this one and rewrite some of the same files. This part only edits the
blocks it owns and names its anchors by content, never by line number, when an earlier batch may
have moved them. Where this part must write an attribute or helper an earlier batch introduced,
it uses the names below; if the earlier batch spelled one differently, keep the earlier batch's
spelling. None of this batch's test assertions depends on these names.

- `<EnvironmentForm>` carries the Batch 1 attributes `:types="page.types"`,
  `v-model:type-edited="typeEdited"` and the boolean prop `type-follows-name` (Add environment and
  the wizard pass it, Edit does not); inside `EnvironmentForm.vue` the type field's reusable
  template component is `<TypeField />`, and the props include `typeFollowsName?: boolean`.
  Batch 1's `environments/Edit.vue` has no `typeEdited` ref (an edited environment's type never
  follows its name).
- `useApplicationWizard()` takes no argument after Batch 1; this batch gives it one parameter,
  `pollInterval`.
- The duration formatters are the registry ones (`formatSeconds`, `formatAgo`). Batch 2 deleted
  `pendingTone`, `waitColor` and `failedTone`; the threshold tone helper is
  `thresholdTone(environment, metric, value)` and the judged failed figure is
  `failedLastHourText(environment)`, both from `components/monitoring/environment/readings.ts`.
  Throughput is written `` `${jobsPerMinute}/min` `` (Batch 2, no translation key).
- Batch 2 added `"Failed · last hour": "Job falliti · ultima ora"` and removed `"Failed"`.
  Batch 4 renamed the banner's `started :elapsed` to `opened :elapsed` (a key that
  `EnvironmentAlerts.vue` and `RecentAlerts.vue` also use) and made the banner's "Rule:" line read
  `formatRule(alert)`.

### Shared names this part introduces (Interfaces)

- PHP: `App\Data\Applications\PollIntervalData::fromConfig(): self` (static constructor on the
  registry class; Batch 7 changes its `step` source when `poll_tick_seconds` becomes a constant).
- Page props: `EnvironmentFormPageData::$pollInterval` and `ApplicationFormPageData::$pollInterval`
  (`PollIntervalData`). The "Edit environment" action reads the existing shared prop
  `canManageApplications` (through `useVisibility()`), so no new page prop is added for it.
- TypeScript: `composables/useBlurConnectionTest.ts` exporting
  `useBlurConnectionTest(payload: () => App.Data.Applications.TestConnectionData, run: () => Promise<void> | void, delayMs?: number): { onUrlBlur: () => void }`;
  `useApplicationWizard(pollInterval: App.Data.Applications.PollIntervalData): ApplicationWizard`
  and `ApplicationWizard.advance: () => void` in `composables/useApplicationWizard.ts`.
- Vue: `EnvironmentForm.vue` gains props `pollInterval`, `editing?`, `storedCredentials?` and the
  emit `urlBlur`; `ReadingFreshness.vue` gains prop `hideReason?: boolean`.
- CSS: `.nc-actions` (the one action row: wraps, right-aligned, secondary then primary). From
  Task 5.13 the shared `components/ui/dialog/DialogFooter.vue` renders it too, so every dialog
  footer is the same row; callers pass no `class` to `<DialogFooter>`.
- Components from the registry created here: `components/FormErrors.vue`,
  `components/DangerZoneCard.vue`. `components/AlertError.vue` is deleted (FormErrors replaces it).

Decisions: the card shows the judged figure exactly as the environment page does,
`failedLastHourText(environment)` ("at least N" when the count is capped, theme 5), toned by

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `app/Data/Applications/PollIntervalData.php`.**

```php
<?php

namespace App\Data\Applications;

use Spatie\LaravelData\Data;

class PollIntervalData extends Data
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $default,
        public int $min,
        public int $max,
        public int $step,
    ) {}

    public static function fromConfig(): self
    {
        return new self(
            default: config()->integer('horizon-watch.readings.poll_interval_seconds.default'),
            min: config()->integer('horizon-watch.readings.poll_interval_seconds.min'),
            max: config()->integer('horizon-watch.readings.poll_interval_seconds.max'),
            step: config()->integer('horizon-watch.readings.poll_tick_seconds'),
        );
    }
}
```

Decisions: the connection test runs 400 ms after the URL field loses focus, only when the address
looks complete (`http(s)://host…`) and only once per distinct URL and credentials; the manual
"Test connection" button stays. The connection test sits on its own line above the action row.
The form is `novalidate` so the server's messages, not the browser's, explain an invalid URL.

**Files:**

- Test: `tests/Feature/PagesAndFormsTest.php`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `ConnectionTest`'s exposed `run()`, `EnvironmentForm` (Task 5.7), `page.pollInterval` (Task 5.6), `.nc-actions` (Task 5.5).
- Produces: `useBlurConnectionTest(payload, run, delayMs = 400): { onUrlBlur }`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing unit test** `resources/js/composables/useBlurConnectionTest.test.ts`:

```ts
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vite-plus/test';
import { useBlurConnectionTest } from '@/composables/useBlurConnectionTest';

const payload = (
    horizonUrl: string,
    basicAuthUser: string | null = null,
): App.Data.Applications.TestConnectionData => ({
    horizonUrl,
    basicAuthUser,
    basicAuthPassword: null,
});

beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
});

afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
});

describe('useBlurConnectionTest', () => {
    it('tests once after the URL field loses focus', () => {
        let current = payload('https://shop.example.com/horizon');
        const run = vi.fn();
        const { onUrlBlur } = useBlurConnectionTest(() => current, run);

        onUrlBlur();
        expect(run).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

        vi.advanceTimersByTime(400);
        expect(run).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();

        onUrlBlur();
        vi.advanceTimersByTime(400);
        expect(run).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();

        current = payload('https://shop.example.com/horizon', 'ops');
        onUrlBlur();
        vi.advanceTimersByTime(400);
        expect(run).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    });

    it('waits for the last of several quick blurs', () => {
        const run = vi.fn();
        const { onUrlBlur } = useBlurConnectionTest(
            () => payload('https://shop.example.com/horizon'),
            run,
        );

        onUrlBlur();
        vi.advanceTimersByTime(200);
        onUrlBlur();
        vi.advanceTimersByTime(200);
        expect(run).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

        vi.advanceTimersByTime(200);
        expect(run).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    });

    it('leaves an empty or incomplete address alone', () => {
        const run = vi.fn();

        for (const url of ['', '   ', 'shop.example.com', 'https://']) {
            useBlurConnectionTest(() => payload(url), run).onUrlBlur();
        }
        vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);

        expect(run).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run it and watch it fail.**
  `docker compose exec -T -u sail laravel.test bash -lc 'npx vp test run resources/js/composables/useBlurConnectionTest.test.ts'`

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `resources/js/composables/useBlurConnectionTest.ts`:

```ts
import { tryOnScopeDispose } from '@vueuse/core';

export type BlurConnectionTest = {
    onUrlBlur: () => void;
};

const COMPLETE_ADDRESS = /^https?:\/\/[^\s/?#]+/i;

export function useBlurConnectionTest(
    payload: () => App.Data.Applications.TestConnectionData,
    run: () => Promise<void> | void,
    delayMs = 400,
): BlurConnectionTest {
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
    let tested = '';

    const onUrlBlur = (): void => {
        clearTimeout(timer);

        timer = setTimeout(() => {
            const current = payload();

            if (!COMPLETE_ADDRESS.test(current.horizonUrl.trim())) {
                return;
            }

            const signature = JSON.stringify(current);

            if (signature === tested) {
                return;
            }

            tested = signature;
            void run();
        }, delayMs);
    };

    tryOnScopeDispose(() => clearTimeout(timer));

    return { onUrlBlur };
}
```

### Task 5.12: Field errors through `InputError`, form-level errors through `FormErrors`

### Task 5.13: Discard changes, destructive triggers, and the remaining forms

Decisions on friction tiers (the existing dialogs already match them): confirm by name for
applications, environments and organizations (`ConfirmByNameDialog`); a simple confirm for removing
a member, leaving an organization, resetting rules and regenerating the signing secret; one click
for revoking an invitation, deleting a maintenance window and removing an unsaved wizard row.
Every confirm button of a destructive dialog is `nc-btn-danger`, as the leave, remove-member and
confirm-by-name dialogs already are; the reset-rules and regenerate-secret dialogs still use
`nc-btn-primary` and change here.
Single-action forms in narrow cards (Invite, the auth pages) keep their full-width button.

Decision on the action row: every form and every dialog ends in one `.nc-actions` row
(right-aligned, wrapping, secondary then primary or danger). The pages Tasks 5.8 to 5.11 rewrote
already use it; this task moves the remaining bespoke rows: the rules form's
`flex flex-wrap items-center justify-end` row, the `ml-auto flex` sub-row of Alert settings (its
Discard changes and Save leave the test-buttons row, which stays a plain tool row, and close the
form), the maintenance form's `.submit` grid cell, the two-factor forms (enable, disable,
regenerate codes, the setup modal's Back / Confirm pair, which stops splitting the width), and the
invitation's Accept / Decline pair (primary first today, so it is reversed). Dialog footers keep
`<DialogFooter>`, which renders `.nc-actions` instead of shadcn's stacked
`flex-col-reverse … sm:justify-end` row, and the `class="gap-2"` callers add becomes redundant.
Batch 6 has no dialog or footer task, so this batch owns them. Header actions (`PageHeader`,
Organizations, first run, the error page) are not form footers and stay as they are. A submit
button outside a row is allowed only as a full-width `nc-btn-block`.

```php
test('every button says what it is, so Enter in a field never presses the wrong one', function () {
    $openingTag = function (string $source, int $at): string {
        $quoted = false;

        for ($i = $at, $length = strlen($source); $i < $length; $i++) {
            if ($source[$i] === '"') {
                $quoted = ! $quoted;
            } elseif ($source[$i] === '>' && ! $quoted) {
                return substr($source, $at, $i - $at + 1);
            }
        }

        return substr($source, $at);
    };

    $untyped = [];

    foreach (pagesAndFormsSources() as $path => $source) {
        preg_match_all('/<button\b/', $source, $found, PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE);

        foreach ($found[0] as [, $at]) {
            if (preg_match('/\s:?type="/', $openingTag($source, $at)) !== 1) {
                $untyped[] = $path;
            }
        }
    }

    expect(array_values(array_unique($untyped)))->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * Each action row of a source (an element whose class starts with `nc-actions`, or a
 * `<DialogFooter>`), as its offset and its markup up to the matching closing tag.
 *
 * @return list<array{int, string}>
 */
function pagesAndFormsActionRows(string $source): array
{
    $rows = [];

    preg_match_all('/<(div|form|Form|DialogFooter)\b(?:[^>"]|"[^"]*")*>/', $source, $tags, PREG_SET_ORDER | PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE);

    foreach ($tags as [[$tag, $at], [$name]]) {
        if ($name !== 'DialogFooter' && preg_match('/\sclass="nc-actions[" ]/', $tag) !== 1) {
            continue;
        }

        preg_match_all('/<(\/?)'.$name.'\b(?:[^>"]|"[^"]*")*>/', $source, $marks, PREG_SET_ORDER | PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE, $at);

        $depth = 0;
        $end = strlen($source);

        foreach ($marks as [[$mark, $offset], [$closing]]) {
            if ($closing === '/') {
                $depth--;
            } elseif (! str_ends_with($mark, '/>')) {
                $depth++;
            }

            if ($depth === 0) {
                $end = $offset + strlen($mark);

                break;
            }
        }

        $rows[] = [$at, substr($source, $at, $end - $at)];
    }

    return $rows;
}

test('every form and dialog ends in one right-aligned action row, secondary then primary', function () {
    expect(pagesAndFormsSource('components/ui/dialog/DialogFooter.vue'))
        ->toContain("cn('nc-actions', props.class)")
        ->not->toContain('flex-col-reverse');

    $misordered = [];
    $outside = [];
    $restyled = [];

    foreach (pagesAndFormsSources() as $path => $source) {
        $rows = pagesAndFormsActionRows($source);

        foreach ($rows as [, $row]) {
            $secondary = strrpos($row, 'nc-btn-secondary');
            $primary = preg_match('/nc-btn-(primary|danger)\b/', $row, $first, PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE) === 1 ? $first[0][1] : false;

            if ($secondary !== false && $primary !== false && $secondary > $primary) {
                $misordered[] = $path;
            }
        }

        if (preg_match('/<DialogFooter\b[^>]*\sclass=/', $source) === 1) {
            $restyled[] = $path;
        }

        preg_match_all('/<button\b(?:[^>"]|"[^"]*")*>/', $source, $buttons, PREG_SET_ORDER | PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE);

        foreach ($buttons as [[$button, $at]]) {
            if (! str_contains($button, 'type="submit"') || str_contains($button, 'nc-btn-block')) {
                continue;
            }

            $inRow = collect($rows)->contains(fn (array $row) => $at > $row[0] && $at < $row[0] + strlen($row[1]));

            if (! $inRow) {
                $outside[] = $path;
            }
        }
    }

    expect(array_values(array_unique($misordered)))->toBe([])
        ->and(array_values(array_unique($outside)))->toBe([])
        ->and($restyled)->toBe([]);

    foreach ([
        'components/monitoring/rules/RulesForm.vue' => 'class="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-end"',
        'components/monitoring/rules/NotificationSettings.vue' => 'class="ml-auto flex"',
        'components/monitoring/rules/MaintenanceWindows.vue' => '.submit',
        'components/TwoFactorSetupModal.vue' => 'class="flex w-full items-center gap-3"',
    ] as $path => $bespoke) {
        expect(pagesAndFormsSource($path))->toContain('class="nc-actions')->not->toContain($bespoke);
    }

    $alertSettings = pagesAndFormsSource('components/monitoring/rules/NotificationSettings.vue');

    expect(strpos($alertSettings, 'class="nc-actions"'))->toBeGreaterThan(strpos($alertSettings, "sendTest('webhook')"));
});
```

  The `every button says what it is` test is a Review Focus pin (see `00-header.md`): this batch
  wraps the wizard, Add and Edit environment, the dialogs and the settings forms in real `<form>`
  elements, and a `<button>` without `type` inside one of them is a submit button, so Enter in a
  field would press it (run the connection test, remove a wizard row, jump a wizard step) before
  the real submit. It passes as soon as it is written, because every button of the tree and of
  this plan has a `type`.

  The action-row test reads each row from its opening tag to its matching closing tag (so a
  nested `<div>` or `<Form>` inside a row is part of it) and holds three rules for every source:
  inside a row no secondary button follows the first primary or danger one; every submit button
  sits inside a row unless it is a full-width `nc-btn-block`; no caller restyles `<DialogFooter>`.
  `components/ui` is outside `pagesAndFormsSources()`, so `DialogFooter.vue` is read on its own.

  Run `docker compose exec -T -u sail laravel.test bash -lc 'php artisan test --compact --filter="Discard changes|danger tone|own submit button|every button says what it is|one right-aligned action row"'`.
  Expected: `Discard changes`, `danger tone`, `own submit button` and `one right-aligned action row`
  fail (the last on `DialogFooter.vue`, which still holds `flex-col-reverse`); `every button says
  what it is` passes.

## Batch 6: Shared primitives and layout

Goal: every screen draws the same concept with the same building block. Status is a circle
(`StatusLamp` in dense rows, `StatusPill` in headers), and both take a missing status plus a label.
An environment is named by `EnvPill`, under its application with `/`. Figures sit in one
`MetricCard` with three sizes. On/off state is an `nc-switch`, picks are an `nc-checkbox`, and the
radio look is for real radios only. Pages with an aside share `.nc-two-col`, form pages share
`.nc-page` + `.nc-page-narrow`, and monitoring detail and form pages open with one `PageHeader`.
The settings screens stop repeating the header bar title. The connection test paints a failure with
one tone, icon and label, in the row header and in the line below. After this batch the ad-hoc
copies (inline dots, the null-status pill, `EnvSwatch`, `KpiCard`, `MetricTile`, the inline stat
tiles, per-page grids and widths, the AlertEmailsToggle private switch) are gone. Source-scanning
guard tests keep them gone.

Spec themes covered: **15** (Shared primitives).

Batch-wide decisions:

- Tasks 6.1–6.9 are committed together, as one commit, at the end of Task 6.10.
- Line numbers come from the tree before Batch 1. Earlier batches move them, so find each site by
  the quoted code, not by the number. Where an earlier batch rewrote the surrounding block, change
  only the element quoted here and keep that batch's bindings and conditions.
- The guard tests live in one new file, `tests/Feature/SharedPrimitivesTest.php`. Each task adds its
  own `test(...)` to it. Its helpers are named `primitiveSources()` and `primitiveFile()`, because
  Pest helpers are global functions and `scriptSources()` / `interfaceFiles()` already exist.
- The front end has no component test runner (no `@vue/test-utils`). Logic that can be unit-tested
  moves into `.ts` modules with Vitest tests. The markup rules are enforced by the PHP source
  guards, like `tests/Feature/AccessibilityTest.php` already does.
- The `/` hierarchy rule applies to the panel interface, including the "Sent notifications" subject
  the server builds for the wall. Server-authored email subjects, the email "where" line and the
  webhook `summary` keep `·`. They are owned by themes 6 and 13, and the spec allows only the
  durations in the webhook `summary` to change.

Assumed from earlier batches (consumed, not produced here):

- Batch 1 (Task 1.7): `EnvPill` props are `{ name: string; type: App.Enums.EnvironmentType; size?: number }`.
  It draws the shield itself when `isProductionType(type)`, and the old `color` / `production`
  props are gone. The TypeScript fields that replaced `color` are, exactly as Batch 1 names them:
  `EnvironmentData.type`, `EnvironmentOptionData.type` (it also replaces `isProduction`),
  `RuleScopeData.type` (nullable), `AlertData.environmentType` (not nullable),
  `MaintenanceWindowData.environmentType` and `MaintenanceTargetData.environmentType` (nullable).
  `lib/monitoring.ts` exports `envTypeColor(type)` in place of `envColor`; `lib/environments.ts`
  exports `isProductionType(type)`. `App.Data.Monitoring.ApplicationData` has
  `domain: string | null`; `EnvironmentFormPageData` has `domain: string | null`, which
  `environments/Create.vue` shows as `page.domain`. Batch 1 already moved `MemberTable.vue`,
  `InviteForm.vue` and `pages/monitoring/environments/Show.vue` to
  `v-if="isProductionType(environment.type)"` with an
  `import { isProductionType } from '@/lib/environments';`, and every `EnvSwatch` that draws an
  alert reads `:type="alert.environmentType"`.
- Batch 2: `readings.ts` exports `statusText(env)`, `statusTone(env)` (a tone for every display
  state, `var(--nc-neutral-500)` for hidden, paused and waiting), `needsAttention(env)`,

```php
<?php

use Symfony\Component\Finder\Finder;

/**
 * @return array<string, string>
 */
function primitiveSources(): array
{
    $files = [];

    foreach (Finder::create()->files()->in(resource_path('js'))->name(['*.vue', '*.ts'])->notName('*.test.ts')->exclude(['generated', 'routes', 'actions', 'wayfinder', 'components/ui']) as $file) {
        $files[$file->getRelativePathname()] = $file->getContents();
    }

    return $files;
}

function primitiveFile(string $path): string
{
    return file_get_contents(resource_path($path));
}

test('the stylesheet carries the shared checkbox, two-column and narrow page primitives', function () {
    expect(primitiveFile('css/nocturne.css'))
        ->toMatch('/\.nc-checkbox \{[^}]*display: inline-flex;/')
        ->toMatch('/\.nc-checkbox \.nc-box \{[^}]*border-radius: var\(--nc-radius-sm\);/')
```

```css
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;

    position: absolute;

    border-color: var(--nc-accent);
    background: var(--nc-accent);

    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    left: 4px;

    outline-offset: 2px;

.nc-checkbox:has(input:disabled) {
    cursor: default;
    color: var(--nc-neutral-500);
}
.nc-checkbox input:disabled + .nc-box {
    opacity: 0.55;
}
```

application list used dots tinted by the environment colour with a status halo, one dot carrying two
facts. They become status lamps labelled "name · state", because the identity colour is not needed
in a row of lamps. The mobile environment header is a header, so its toned lamp-plus-text span
(an ad-hoc pill without a border) becomes the same `StatusPill` as the desktop header.

Create `resources/js/components/nocturne/status.ts`:

```ts
import { trans } from 'laravel-vue-i18n';
import { statusColor, statusLabel } from '@/lib/monitoring';

export function lampColor(
    status: App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus | null,
    tone?: string,
): string {
    if (tone) {
        return tone;
    }

    return status === null ? 'var(--nc-neutral-500)' : statusColor(status);
}

export function lampLabel(
    status: App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus | null,
    label?: string,
): string {
    if (label) {
        return label;
    }

    return status === null ? trans('No reading yet') : statusLabel(status);
}
```

### Task 6.5: Booleans: `nc-switch` for on/off, `nc-checkbox` for options, `nc-radio` for radios

**Files:**

- Modify: `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.vue` (lines 69–73)
- Modify: `resources/js/components/settings/AlertEmailsToggle.vue` (template lines 36–51, delete the `<style scoped>` block lines 53–122)
- Test: `tests/Feature/SharedPrimitivesTest.php`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `.nc-switch` / `.nc-track` (existing), `.nc-checkbox` / `.nc-box` (Task 6.1).
- Produces: none.

Rule enforced by the guard: every `<input type="checkbox">` sits in a `<label>` whose class holds
`nc-switch` (and then the input has `role="switch"`), or `nc-checkbox` (and then it has no
`role="switch"`). `nc-radio` remains on the real radios of `InviteForm.vue` (role picker).
Batch 1's `TypePicker.vue` is a real radio group too (`role="radiogroup"`, hidden
`<input type="radio">`) with its own chip style; leave it as it is. `EnvironmentForm.vue` needs no change here: Task 5.7 already made "Collect
readings" and "Basic auth" `nc-switch` labels, and the production checkbox went with Batch 1. The
`RuleRow.vue` switches (`nc-switch check nc-t-xs`, `role="switch"`) and the member pickers (Task
6.3) already pass.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing guard test**

Append to `tests/Feature/SharedPrimitivesTest.php`:

```php
test('a checkbox is a switch for on and off, or a checkbox for picks, never the radio look', function () {
    $wrong = [];

    foreach (primitiveSources() as $path => $source) {
        $offset = 0;

        while (($at = strpos($source, 'type="checkbox"', $offset)) !== false) {
            $offset = $at + 1;
            $before = substr($source, 0, $at);

            $labelAt = strrpos($before, '<label');
            $label = $labelAt === false ? '' : substr($source, $labelAt, strpos($source, '>', $labelAt) - $labelAt);

            $inputAt = (int) strrpos($before, '<input');
            $input = substr($source, $inputAt, strpos($source, '/>', $at) - $inputAt);

            $switch = str_contains($label, 'nc-switch') && str_contains($input, 'role="switch"');
            $checkbox = str_contains($label, 'nc-checkbox') && ! str_contains($input, 'role="switch"');

            if (! $switch && ! $checkbox) {
                $wrong[] = $path;
            }
        }
    }

    expect(array_values(array_unique($wrong)))->toBe([]);
});
```

Expected: FAIL. `$wrong` is `['components/settings/AlertEmailsToggle.vue', 'pages/auth/Login.vue']` (in Finder order; the assertion only needs it empty).

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `connection.ts`**

Create `resources/js/components/monitoring/applications/connection.ts`:

```ts
import {
    PhCheckCircle,
    PhCircleNotch,
    PhHourglassMedium,
    PhMinusCircle,
    PhWarning,
} from '@phosphor-icons/vue';
import { trans, transChoice } from 'laravel-vue-i18n';
import type { Component } from 'vue';
import {
    horizonStatusLabel,
    readingErrorLabel,
} from '@/components/monitoring/environment/readings';

export type ConnectionOutcome =
    | { state: 'idle' }
    | { state: 'testing' }
    | { state: 'done'; result: App.Data.Monitoring.ConnectionResultData }
    | { state: 'throttled' }
    | { state: 'invalid'; message: string }
    | { state: 'failed' };

export function connectionTone(outcome: ConnectionOutcome): string {
    switch (outcome.state) {
        case 'idle':
            return 'var(--nc-neutral-500)';
        case 'testing':
            return 'var(--nc-neutral-400)';
        case 'done':
            return outcome.result.reachable ? 'var(--st-ok)' : 'var(--st-down)';
        case 'throttled':
            return 'var(--st-warn)';
        case 'invalid':
        case 'failed':
            return 'var(--st-down)';
    }
}

export function connectionIcon(outcome: ConnectionOutcome): Component {
    switch (outcome.state) {
        case 'idle':
            return PhMinusCircle;
        case 'testing':
            return PhCircleNotch;
        case 'done':
            return outcome.result.reachable ? PhCheckCircle : PhWarning;
        case 'throttled':
            return PhHourglassMedium;
        case 'invalid':
        case 'failed':
            return PhWarning;
    }
}

export function connectionState(outcome: ConnectionOutcome): string {
    switch (outcome.state) {
        case 'testing':
            return trans('Testing…');
        case 'done':
            return outcome.result.reachable
                ? trans('Connected')
                : trans('Not connected');
        default:
            return trans('Not tested');
    }
}

export function connectionMessage(outcome: ConnectionOutcome): string | null {
    switch (outcome.state) {
        case 'idle':
            return null;
        case 'testing':
            return trans('Testing the connection…');
        case 'throttled':
            return trans('Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.');
        case 'invalid':
            return outcome.message;
        case 'failed':
            return trans(
                'The test could not run. Reload the page and try again.',
            );
        case 'done':
            return resultMessage(outcome.result);
    }
}

function resultMessage(
    result: App.Data.Monitoring.ConnectionResultData,
): string {
    if (result.reachable) {
        return transChoice(
            'Connected · Horizon :status · :count master · :ms ms|Connected · Horizon :status · :count masters · :ms ms',
            result.masterCount ?? 0,
            {
                status: result.horizonStatus
                    ? horizonStatusLabel(result.horizonStatus)
                    : '—',
                ms: String(result.latencyMs ?? 0),
            },
        );
    }

    return result.error
        ? readingErrorLabel(result.error)
        : trans('The test could not run. Reload the page and try again.');
}
```

## Batch 7: Data and payload trimming

Goal: remove stored data and props that only repeat something the product already knows. Two alert
columns are always derivable (`alerts.notified` from `last_notified_at`, `alerts.unit` from the
metric). `users.email_verified_at` belongs to a feature the product does not have. The shared
`auth.user` and two pages send props that no page reads. Two "tunables" have only one safe value.
The client keeps its own copy of the status severity order. After this batch each of these facts has
one source. The webhook v1 payload keeps its `unit` key through a model accessor. The CHANGELOG
upgrade note for the dropped columns belongs to Batch 8 (theme 19), not to this batch.

Spec themes covered: **17** (Data and payload trimming: new migrations, page props, config
constants, severity order, settings routes).

Batch-wide decisions:

- New migrations are numbered `2026_10_16_000004` and `2026_10_16_000005`, continuing Batch 1's
  `000001`–`000003` as Batch 1's Interfaces block asks ("later batches number their `2026_10_16_*`
  migrations from `000004`"). No batch between 2 and 6 adds a migration, so these sort right after
  Batch 1's and are the two newest when Task 7.8 rolls them back.
- Tasks 7.1–7.7 are committed together, as one commit, at the end of Task 7.8.
- The line numbers below come from the tree before Batch 1. Earlier batches move them, so find each
  site by the quoted code, not by the number.

- Produces (registry): `Alert::wasNotified(): bool`, which is `last_notified_at !== null`. Also the read-only accessor `Alert::$unit`, which returns `$this->metric->unit()`. `AlertData.unit`, `WebhookPayload` `alert.unit` and `AlertMail` keep reading `$alert->unit` without change.

Decision: before the drop, the migration gives every row with `notified = true` and
`last_notified_at IS NULL` the value `last_notified_at = opened_at`. The code never writes such a
row. If one exists, it stays "notified", so its resolution is still announced. Its next repeat may
come early, which is the safe side.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the migration**

Create `database/migrations/2026_10_16_000004_drop_derived_columns_from_alerts_table.php`:

```php
<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        DB::table('alerts')
            ->where('notified', true)
            ->whereNull('last_notified_at')
            ->update(['last_notified_at' => DB::raw('opened_at')]);

        Schema::table('alerts', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->dropColumn(['notified', 'unit']);
        });
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        Schema::table('alerts', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->boolean('notified')->default(false);
            $table->string('unit', 8)->nullable();
        });

        DB::statement('update alerts set notified = (last_notified_at is not null)');
        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            update alerts set unit = case metric
                when 'horizon.master_inactive' then 'min'
                when 'endpoint.unreachable' then 'min'
                when 'horizon.paused' then 'min'
                when 'queue.pending' then 'job'
                when 'jobs.failed_per_hour' then 'job'
                when 'queue.max_wait' then 's'
                when 'job.runtime' then 's'
                else ''
            end
            SQL);

        Schema::table('alerts', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->string('unit', 8)->nullable(false)->change();
        });
    }
};
```

The `case` hard-codes `AlertRuleMetric::unit()` as it is on 2026-10-16. A migration must not follow
later changes to the enum.

### Task 7.6: The worst status comes from the server; delete the client severity order

**Files:**

- Modify: `app/Enums/EnvironmentStatus.php` (add `worstOf()` after `severity()`)
- Modify: `app/Data/Pages/ApplicationGroupData.php` (add `worstStatus` after Batch 2's `attentionCount`)
- Modify: `app/Queries/ApplicationListQuery.php` (the `array_map` callback, as Batch 2 left it)
- Modify: `resources/js/components/monitoring/AttentionBadge.vue` (created by Batch 2, Task 2.7: script block)
- Modify: `resources/js/components/monitoring/wall/ApplicationGroup.vue` (Batch 2's script and its `AttentionBadge` call)
- Modify: `resources/js/components/monitoring/applications/ApplicationSection.vue` (Batch 2's `AttentionBadge` call)
- Modify: `resources/js/components/mobile/applications/ApplicationList.vue` (Batch 2's `AttentionBadge` call)
- Modify: `resources/js/components/monitoring/environment/readings.ts` (delete `SEVERITY` and `worstTone`, old lines 47–64)
- Modify (tests): `tests/Unit/EnvironmentStatusTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Monitoring/ApplicationPagesTest.php`, `tests/Feature/InterfaceComponentsTest.php`, `resources/js/components/monitoring/environment/readings.test.ts` (delete `describe('worstTone')`)

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `EnvironmentStatus::severity()` (unchanged), `EnvironmentData::compareBySeverityThenPending` (unchanged; `WallQuery::handle()` already sorts `page.environments` with it). From Batch 2: `EnvironmentData::needsAttention(): bool` (PHP), `ApplicationGroupData::$attentionCount`, `needsAttention(env)` from `readings.ts`, and `AttentionBadge.vue` with props `{ count: number; environments: App.Data.Monitoring.EnvironmentData[] }`, which today tones itself through `worstTone(environments.filter(needsAttention))`.
- Produces (**new shared names**): `EnvironmentStatus::worstOf(iterable<EnvironmentStatus|null> $statuses): ?EnvironmentStatus` and `ApplicationGroupData::$worstStatus` (`?EnvironmentStatus`; TS `worstStatus: App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus | null`). `AttentionBadge.vue` props become `{ count: number; worstStatus: App.Enums.EnvironmentStatus | null }` (the `environments` prop goes). `worstTone` and `SEVERITY` are deleted from `readings.ts`.

Decisions:

- The application list sends `worstStatus` per group, computed over the same environments as `attentionCount` (those whose `needsAttention()` is true), so the tone and the number always describe the same set.
- The wall builds its groups on the client from `page.environments`, which `WallQuery` sends worst first (`usort($environments, EnvironmentData::compareBySeverityThenPending(...))`; `Wall.vue`'s `shown` and `groups` computeds only filter and bucket, so each group keeps that order; `WallTest`'s "an application first appears on the wall at its worst environment" pins the order). So a wall group's worst status is the status of its first environment that needs attention and has a status, and it follows the wall filters. The client needs no severity order. Decision: skip environments without a status (`find(… status !== null)`, not `[0]`), because `EnvironmentData::severity()` sorts a missing status between `degraded` and `active`; a troubled environment without a status (a reading error before any reading) can then come before a statused one, and `worstTone` ignored it too. This gives the same tone as Batch 2's `worstTone(troubled)` in every case.
- `ApplicationDetailPageData::$worstStatus` already comes from the server and stays as it is.

In `app/Enums/EnvironmentStatus.php`, add after `severity()`:

```php
    /**
     * @param  iterable<self|null>  $statuses
     */
    public static function worstOf(iterable $statuses): ?self
    {
        $worst = null;

        foreach ($statuses as $status) {
            if ($status !== null && ($worst === null || $status->severity() < $worst->severity())) {
                $worst = $status;
            }
        }

        return $worst;
    }
```

### Task 8.5: Bare version in `Version::current()`

Decision: `Version::current()` drops a leading `v` only when a digit follows (`v1.0.0` → `1.0.0`,
`v1.1.0-rc.1` → `1.1.0-rc.1`), so a hand-built image passed `VERSION=v1.2.3` also reports the
bare form, and words such as `vnext` or `dev` are kept. The test fixtures move to the bare
`1.0.0`, which is what the release workflow passes from Task 8.6 on.

**Files:**

- Modify: `app/Support/Version.php` (`current()`, lines 7-12)
- Test: `tests/Feature/VersionTest.php` (lines 8-40)
- Modify (fixtures `v1.0.0` → `1.0.0`): `tests/Feature/Horizon/HorizonClientTest.php` (lines 201,
  222), `tests/Feature/Monitoring/PanelHealthTest.php` (lines 66, 79, 255, 269),
  `tests/Feature/Alerts/WebhookClientTest.php` (lines 91, 108)

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: config `horizon-watch.version` (`HORIZON_WATCH_VERSION`).
- Produces: `App\Support\Version::current(): string` never starts with `v` followed by a digit;
  `Version::userAgent()` follows (`HorizonWatch/1.0.0`). Batch 9's `app_version` reads it.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Replace the first test of `tests/Feature/VersionTest.php` (lines 8-21) with these two:

```php

    expect(config('horizon-watch.version'))->toBe('dev')
        ->and(Version::current())->toBe('dev')
        ->and(Version::userAgent())->toBe('HorizonWatch/dev');

    config(['horizon-watch.version' => '1.0.0']);

    expect(Version::current())->toBe('1.0.0')
        ->and(Version::userAgent())->toBe('HorizonWatch/1.0.0');

    config(['horizon-watch.version' => ' ']);

    expect(Version::current())->toBe('dev');
});

test('a version built from a git tag is shown without the v of the tag', function (string $built, string $shown) {
    config(['horizon-watch.version' => $built]);

    expect(Version::current())->toBe($shown)
        ->and(Version::userAgent())->toBe("HorizonWatch/{$shown}");
})->with([
    'stable tag' => ['v1.0.0', '1.0.0'],
    'pre-release tag' => ['v1.1.0-rc.1', '1.1.0-rc.1'],
    'already bare' => ['1.0.0', '1.0.0'],
    'a word that starts with v' => ['vnext', 'vnext'],

```

```php
    public static function current(): string
```
